$wn.ColPlan = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  R15: the column plan of a grid, pure arithmetic: the smallest width and the fill weight of each column (R28 finding 4).
  .DESCRIPTION
  Every column fills: a column keeps at most its own width as its minimum, and all minimums together never exceed the
  room the grid has: the grid width less the vertical scroll bar ($wn.BarW; R15: kept in every grid, whether the bar
  shows or not) and 2 px, so the visible columns never end under the bar.
  R7 (R32 W1): a pub column keeps its whole minimum, $PubMin (its widest number, title and head plus the cell padding),
  so a number is never cut; the other columns share what is left (their text wraps).
  R8 (R35 W7): each other column keeps at least its head ($wn.HeadMin) when all heads fit: it wants the larger of its
  own width and its head; when all wants do not fit, each gets its head and the rest is shared by what it wanted more.
  Only when the heads alone do not fit do the columns shrink by one factor as before (the self-check names a cut head).
  R11 (R38): a column that is not the pub column wants the narrower of its declared width and its widest value, so a
  short column gives its room away; a chip column wants its widest chip (never less) and keeps it whole when the room is
  short, like the pub column; the fill weight of a column is the width it wants.
  .PARAMETER Cols
  The column list: N, W (0 = takes the rest), K, H.
  .PARAMETER W
  The grid width.
  .PARAMETER Scroll
  The width of the vertical scroll bar when the grid scrolls, else 0 (the fill weight of the column that takes the rest).
  .PARAMETER PubMin
  The smallest width of a pub column ($wn.PubMin), or 0.
  .PARAMETER Rows
  R11: all the rows of the grid, to measure each column's widest value ($wn.ValueMin); none: the declared widths.
  .OUTPUTS
  @{ Min = the smallest width by column name, in column order; Weight = the fill weight by name; Room = the room the
  minimums share; Reserve = the grid width less that room ($wn.FitGrid keeps it); ChipKept = $true or $false when the grid has a chip column (its chip kept whole), else $null }.
  #>
  param($Cols, [int]$W, [int]$Scroll, [int]$PubMin, $Rows = @())
  # R15: the room for the scroll bar is kept in every grid (r14: only with a pub column). ps51 W7 (96 dpi, narrowest page):
  # a grid with no pub column and no bar showing gives that room to its heads when only then they all fit (as r14).
  $bar = [math]::Max($Scroll, [int](& $wn.BarW)); $heads = 0; foreach ($c in $Cols) { $heads += [int](& $wn.HeadMin $c) }
  if ($PubMin -le 0 -and $Scroll -eq 0 -and $heads -gt $W - $bar - 2 -and $heads -le $W - 2) { $bar = 0 }
  $fixed = 0; $keep = 0; $rest = 0; $n = @($Cols).Count; $avail = $W - $bar - 2; $kept = $null
  $pubOwn = [math]::Max(2, [math]::Min([math]::Max((& $wn.Sc 60), $PubMin), $avail - 2 * ($n - 1)))   # a pub column never leaves less than 2 px a column
  $own = @{}; $hard = @{}; $spare = & $wn.HeadSpare $Cols $avail $PubMin $pubOwn; foreach ($c in $Cols) {   # R11: a chip is kept only while the heads fit
    $isPub = ($c.K -eq 'pub' -and $PubMin -gt 0); $vm = $(if (@($Rows).Count) { [int](& $wn.ValueMin $c $Rows) } else { 0 })
    $chipKeep = ($c.K -eq 'chip' -and $vm -gt 0 -and ($vm - [int](& $wn.HeadMin $c)) -le $spare)   # Tag.ChipKept: the edge check judges only a kept chip
    if ($c.K -eq 'chip') { $kept = $chipKeep; if ($chipKeep) { $spare -= [math]::Max(0, $vm - [int](& $wn.HeadMin $c)) } }
    $hard[[string]$c.N] = ($isPub -or $chipKeep)
    $o = $(if ($isPub) { $pubOwn } elseif ($chipKeep) { [math]::Max($vm, [int](& $wn.HeadMin $c)) } elseif ($c.W -eq 0) { & $wn.Sc 60 }
      elseif ($vm -gt 0) { [math]::Min((& $wn.Sc $c.W), $vm) } else { & $wn.Sc $c.W }); $own[[string]$c.N] = $o
    if ($c.W -ne 0) { $fixed += $o }; if ($hard[[string]$c.N]) { $keep += $o } else { $rest += $o } }
  $k = $(if ($rest -gt 0 -and $keep + $rest -gt $avail) { [math]::Max(0.0, [double]($avail - $keep) / $rest) } else { 1.0 })
  # R8 (W7): the head floor of each other column, what it wants, and the room they share ($avail less the pub column)
  $hm = @{}; $want = 0; $floor = 0; $more = 0
  foreach ($c in $Cols) { if (-not $hard[[string]$c.N]) { $f = & $wn.HeadMin $c; $hm[[string]$c.N] = $f
      $floor += $f; $want += [math]::Max($own[[string]$c.N], $f); $more += [math]::Max(0, $own[[string]$c.N] - $f) } }
  $pool = $avail - $keep
  $mins = [ordered]@{}; $wts = @{}
  foreach ($c in $Cols) {
    $o = $own[[string]$c.N]; $f = [int]$hm[[string]$c.N]
    $mins[[string]$c.N] = [int]$(if ($hard[[string]$c.N]) { $o } elseif ($want -le $pool) { [math]::Max($o, $f) }
      elseif ($floor -le $pool) { $f + $(if ($more -gt 0) { [int][math]::Floor(($pool - $floor) * [math]::Max(0, $o - $f) / [double]$more) } else { 0 }) }
      else { [math]::Max(2, [int][math]::Floor($o * $k)) })
    $wts[[string]$c.N] = [single]$(if ($c.W -eq 0) { [math]::Max(60, $W - $fixed - $Scroll) } else { [math]::Max(1, $o) }) }
  return @{ Min = $mins; Weight = $wts; Room = $avail; Reserve = $W - $avail; ChipKept = $kept } }
# Adds the columns of the plan ($wn.ColPlan; the parameters are its own) to grid $G: each fills, with its smallest width
# and its fill weight. Gives back the column kinds by name (@{ name = kind }); $wn.ChipKept is the plan's ChipKept.
$wn.GridCols = {
  param($G, $Cols, [int]$W, [int]$Scroll, [int]$PubMin, $Rows = @())
  $plan = & $wn.ColPlan $Cols $W $Scroll $PubMin $Rows; $wn.ChipKept = $plan.ChipKept; $wn.Reserve = $plan.Reserve
  $kinds = @{}
  foreach ($c in $Cols) {
    $dc = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.DataGridViewTextBoxColumn; $dc.Name = [string]$c.N; $dc.HeaderText = $(if ($c.H) { [string]$c.H } else { [string]$c.N }); $dc.SortMode = 'NotSortable'
    $dc.AutoSizeMode='Fill'; $dc.MinimumWidth = [math]::Max(2, [int]$plan.Min[[string]$c.N]); $dc.FillWeight = $plan.Weight[[string]$c.N]
    [void]$G.Columns.Add($dc); $kinds[[string]$c.N] = [string]$c.K }
  return $kinds }
# R15: the width of a vertical scroll bar ($wn.BarW) and of the bar grid $G shows now, else 0 ($wn.BarShown), in px.
$wn.BarW = { return [int][Windows.Forms.SystemInformation]::VerticalScrollBarWidth }
# R15: the width of the vertical scroll bar that grid $G shows now (0 when none shows); $wn.FitGrid and $wn.EdgeCheck use it.
$wn.BarShown = { param($G) $v = @($G.Controls | Where-Object { $_ -is [Windows.Forms.VScrollBar] -and $_.Visible }); if ($v.Count) { return [int]$v[0].Width }; return 0 }
# R11 (R38; ps51 W7 at 96 dpi): the room a grid of width $Avail has above all its column heads (the pub column counts
# $PubOwn when $PubMin is above 0). $wn.GridCols keeps a status chip whole only while that room holds the chip's extra
# width, else the chip column shares the room as in r10, so a narrow window never cuts the other heads.
$wn.HeadSpare = { param($Cols, [int]$Avail, [int]$PubMin, [int]$PubOwn)
  $spare = $Avail; foreach ($c in $Cols) { $spare -= $(if ($c.K -eq 'pub' -and $PubMin -gt 0) { $PubOwn } else { [int](& $wn.HeadMin $c) }) }
  return $spare }
# R11 (R38; the PFM, 20 Nov 26: "hide Since when narrow"): the columns of a grid of width $W with each column marked Drop
# left out, last first, while the pub column's minimum ($wn.PubMin of the widths $Pw) and every other whole head do not fit
# beside the scroll bar. Wide windows keep every column.
# R12 (R38 finding 2: the Your Work grid needed 957 px and had 935 at 150 %): a chip column counts its widest chip of
# $Rows ($wn.ValueMin), not only its head, so Since leaves when the whole chips do not fit beside the other heads.
$wn.DropCols = { param($Cols, [int]$W, $Pw, $Rows = @())
  $cols = @($Cols); $avail = $W - (& $wn.BarW) - 2
  while ($true) {
    $need = [int](& $wn.PubMin $cols $Pw)
    foreach ($c in $cols) { if ($c.K -ne 'pub') { $hm = [int](& $wn.HeadMin $c)
        $sb = [math]::Max((& $ui.Sc 10), [int](& $wn.BarW))   # ValueMin keeps a scroll bar right of a chip; $avail has taken it off already
        $need += $(if ($c.K -eq 'chip' -and @($Rows).Count) { [math]::Max($hm, [int](& $wn.ValueMin $c $Rows) - $sb) } else { $hm }) } }
    $drop = @($cols | Where-Object { $_.Drop }) | Select-Object -Last 1
    if ($need -le $avail -or -not $drop) { return ,$cols }
    $cols = @($cols | Where-Object { $_ -ne $drop }) } }
$wn.Grid = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  A grid block: the grid with its columns, rows, painted cells and keys; with Count, the line under it that counts the rows.
  .PARAMETER Parent
  The card that gets the grid.
  .PARAMETER b
  The grid block: Name, Rows, Cols, ColsWide (used when the window is wide and they fit), Fill, Count.
  .PARAMETER W
  The grid width.
  .PARAMETER Ctx
  The column context (for Fill).
  #>
  param($Parent, $b, [int]$W, $Ctx)
  $cols = @($b.Cols)
  if ($wn.Wide -and $b.ColsWide) { $wf = 0; foreach ($c in $b.ColsWide) { $wf += (& $wn.Sc $c.W) }; if ($wf + (& $wn.Sc 137) -le $W) { $cols = @($b.ColsWide) } }
  $rows = @($b.Rows); $pw = & $wn.PubWidths $rows; $cols = & $wn.DropCols $cols $W $pw $rows; $hs = & $wn.GridHeight $b $Ctx
  $g = & $wn.GridNew ([string]$b.Name) $W $hs
  $scroll = $(if ($hs.Full -gt $hs.H) { (& $wn.BarW) } else { 0 })
  $wn.ChipKept = $null; $kinds = & $wn.GridCols $g $cols $W $scroll (& $wn.PubMin $cols $pw) $rows
  $chipKind = @{}; foreach ($r in $rows) { if ($r.Status) { $chipKind[[string]$r.Status] = [string]$r.Kind } }
  $g.Tag = @{ Kind = $kinds; Chip = $chipKind; Cols = $cols; Shown = $rows; PubW = $pw.Num; PubT = $pw.Title; PubGap = (& $ui.Sc 6); Drawn = @{}; Head = $null
    Heads = [ordered]@{}; ChipKept = $wn.ChipKept; Reserve = $wn.Reserve }
  & $wn.GridFill $g $rows
  $g.Add_CellPainting({ param($s, $e) & $wn.PaintCell $s $e })
  $g.Add_CellDoubleClick({ param($s, $e) if ($e.RowIndex -ge 0) { & $wn.Later $s $e.RowIndex } })
  $g.Add_KeyDown({ param($s, $e) if ($e.KeyCode -eq 'Return') { $e.Handled = $true; $e.SuppressKeyPress = $true; if ($s.CurrentRow) { & $wn.Later $s $s.CurrentRow.Index } } })
  [void]$Parent.Controls.Add($g); $g.ClearSelection(); $wn.Gridsel = $g
  # R18 (the PFM, 26 Nov 26, R45 comment 4: a stray label "4" under the waves grid): the Count property of a hash table is its number of keys (the 4 keys
  # of the waves block), never "no Count key", so the line under the grid showed that number. The key is read by name, with an index.
  $cnt = [string]$b['Count']
  if ($cnt) { $wn.CountText = $cnt; $wn.CountBox = & $wn.Txt $Parent ($cnt -f $rows.Count) $ui.F.Small $ui.C.Gray 8 $W 'Count' $null; $wn.Gridq = $g } }
# R10 (R37; R36 finding 3: the home grid "Who has it now" columns needed 810 px, the grid had 801): after a card is laid
# out, each grid on the page whose column minimums are wider than its room gives the excess back ($wn.FitGrid). The
# layout self-check ($wn.ScrollCheck) still measures the result, so a grid that does not fit stays a defect. Gives back
# the number of grids changed.
$wn.FitGrids = {
  $n = 0; $st = New-Object System.Collections.Stack; $st.Push($page)
  while ($st.Count) { foreach ($c in $st.Pop().Controls) {
      if ($c -is [Windows.Forms.DataGridView]) { if (& $wn.FitGrid $c) { $n++ } }
      elseif ($c.Controls.Count) { $st.Push($c) } } }
  return $n }
$wn.FitGrid = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  R10, R15: fits one grid (see $wn.FitGrids): lowers column minimums by the excess of the minimums over the grid's room.
  .DESCRIPTION
  R15 (R41 finding 4): the room is the client width less the plan's reserve (Tag.Reserve, $wn.ColPlan) or less the bar
  that shows now, the larger; the excess is the sum of the minimums of the visible columns less the room, so a grid
  that fits gives nothing back however its fill columns share the width. The excess comes off the columns that are not the pub column, the one with the most width above its head
  ($wn.HeadMin) first: the other columns above their heads, then the chip column above its head, then any column under
  its head (never under 2 px). When the minimums changed, or the filled columns end past the grid or under a bar that shows, the grid lays
  out its columns again (a 1 px size change makes the fill columns share the room again).
  R16 (R42 finding 2): when the columns still end past the grid, or under a bar that shows, after that layout, their widths
  are cut to the room ($wn.TrimWidths).
  R15 (R42 ps51 keep test: a later open of the Wave 1 answers card took 114 ms, 13 before): when the fit took off a bar
  that shows beyond the plan's reserve, Tag.Reserve becomes that bar and the columns keep their widths (AutoSizeMode
  None): their fill width no longer depends on the bar, and the bar no longer on the row heights the widths give, so a
  second fit, and a later open of the kept card, find nothing to do.
  .PARAMETER G
  The grid (its Tag holds the column kinds and the column list, $wn.Grid); any object with ClientSize, Width, Columns
  (Name, Visible, Width, MinimumWidth, AutoSizeMode) and that Tag (tests/check_t22_r18.py gives one off Windows).
  .OUTPUTS
  $true when it changed a column or laid the grid out again, else $false.
  #>
  param($G)
  # the plan's room (Tag.Reserve), and never under a vertical bar that shows now (rows that wrap can bring one)
  $res = $(if ($null -ne $G.Tag.Reserve) { [int]$G.Tag.Reserve } else { [int](& $wn.BarW) + 2 })
  $shown = [int](& $wn.BarShown $G); $room = [int]$G.ClientSize.Width - [math]::Max($res, $shown)
  $vis = @($G.Columns | Where-Object { $_.Visible }); $mins = 0; $sum = 0
  foreach ($k in $vis) { $mins += [int]$k.MinimumWidth; $sum += [int]$k.Width }
  $excess = $mins - $room; $stale = ($sum -gt [int]$G.ClientSize.Width - $shown + 1)   # stale: the filled widths end past the grid or under a bar that shows
  if ($excess -le 0 -and -not $stale) { return $false }
  $kinds = $G.Tag.Kind; $heads = @{}; foreach ($c in @($G.Tag.Cols)) { $heads[[string]$c.N] = [int](& $wn.HeadMin $c) }
  $free = @($vis | Where-Object { [string]$kinds[$_.Name] -ne 'pub' }); $gave = 0
  foreach ($pass in 'others above head', 'above head', 'under head') {
    $set = @($free | Where-Object { $pass -ne 'others above head' -or [string]$kinds[$_.Name] -ne 'chip' })
    foreach ($k in @($set | Sort-Object { [int]$_.MinimumWidth - [int]$heads[$_.Name] } -Descending)) {
      if ($excess -le 0) { break }
      $floor = $(if ($pass -eq 'under head') { 2 } else { [math]::Max(2, [int]$heads[$k.Name]) })
      $give = [math]::Min($excess, [int]$k.MinimumWidth - $floor); if ($give -le 0) { continue }
      $k.MinimumWidth = [int]$k.MinimumWidth - $give; $excess -= $give; $gave++ } }
  if (-not $gave -and -not $stale) { return $false }   # excess, but no column could give any width back: nothing changed
  $G.Width = $G.Width - 1; $G.Width = $G.Width + 1   # the fill columns share the room again
  # R16 (R42 finding 2: home and queue still "columns need 979, the grid has 961" and "1442, 1428"): the minimums fitted, so the
  # excess above was 0, and the layout above gave the same widths again. The widths themselves are cut to the room here.
  $null = & $wn.TrimWidths $vis $room ([int]$G.ClientSize.Width - $shown)   # R16 review: a bar that shows counts, also under the grid width
  if ($shown -gt $res) {   # R15: the grid keeps the room of the bar that shows, and its widths stop following the bar
    $G.Tag.Reserve = $shown; foreach ($k in $vis) { $k.AutoSizeMode = 'None' } }   # (no fill and row layout again on each open)
  return $true }
# R16 (R42 finding 2): after the grid laid its fill columns out, cuts their widths to $Room when they still end past the grid
# (they end past $Client: the grid width less the bar that shows, 1 px of rounding allowed): the width above its column minimum comes off, the column with the most first, and
# the columns stop filling (AutoSizeMode None), so the grid's own layout cannot give the width back. No column goes under its
# minimum, so a kept status chip keeps its whole width ($wn.ValueMin). $Cols: the visible columns (Width, MinimumWidth,
# AutoSizeMode). Gives back $true when it changed a width, else $false.
$wn.TrimWidths = { param($Cols, [int]$Room, [int]$Client)
  $sum = 0; foreach ($k in $Cols) { $sum += [int]$k.Width }
  if ($sum -le $Client + 1) { return $false }   # the widths end before the bar that shows (or the grid edge): nothing to cut
  $over = $sum - $Room; foreach ($k in $Cols) { $k.AutoSizeMode = 'None' }
  foreach ($k in @($Cols | Sort-Object { [int]$_.Width - [int]$_.MinimumWidth } -Descending)) {
    if ($over -le 0) { break }
    $give = [math]::Min($over, [int]$k.Width - [int]$k.MinimumWidth); if ($give -le 0) { continue }
    $k.Width = [int]$k.Width - $give; $over -= $give }
  return $true }
# The widest number (as a link) and the widest title of the pub values ("number|title") of $Rows, in pixels, measured as
# $wn.PaintPub draws them. All rows, not only the shown ones, so a filter does not move the title column.
$wn.PubWidths = { param($Rows)
  $out = @{ Num = 0; Title = 0 }   # R15: measured by $wn.TextW (the same flags), so the column plan runs off Windows too
  foreach ($r in @($Rows)) { $pp = ([string]$r.Publication).Split('|'); if ($pp.Count -lt 2) { continue }
    $out.Num = [math]::Max($out.Num, [int](& $wn.TextW $pp[0] $ui.F.Link))
    $out.Title = [math]::Max($out.Title, [int](& $wn.TextW $pp[1] $ui.F.Small)) }
  return $out }
# The width of a one-line text $Text in font $F as the grid draws it (no padding), in pixels.
$wn.TextW = { param([string]$Text, $F)
  return [Windows.Forms.TextRenderer]::MeasureText($Text, $F, ([Drawing.Size]::new(100000, 0)), [Windows.Forms.TextFormatFlags]'NoPadding, NoPrefix').Width }
# The head text of grid column $C as the grid draws it: its header text (H, else its name) in capitals.
$wn.HeadText = { param($C) return ($(if ($C.H) { [string]$C.H } else { [string]$C.N })).ToUpperInvariant() }
# R8 (R35 W7): the smallest width of grid column $C that shows its whole head: the head text in the head font, the cell
# padding at both sides ($wn.PaintCell) and 1 px, as $wn.PubMin does for the pub column.
# R11: a column marked HW has a head that may wrap to 2 lines: its head width is that of the wider of the 2 lines.
$wn.HeadMin = { param($C) return ((& $(if ($C.HW) { $wn.HeadWrap } else { $wn.HeadW1 }) $C) + 2 * (& $ui.Sc 10) + 1) }
# The width of the head of column $C on one line, in pixels.
$wn.HeadW1 = { param($C) return (& $wn.TextW (& $wn.HeadText $C) $ui.F.SmallB) }
# R11: the narrowest width the head of column $C shows in at most 2 lines, breaking between words: the best split into
# 2 lines, the width of its wider line; the one-line width when the head is one word.
$wn.HeadWrap = { param($C)
  $words = @((& $wn.HeadText $C) -split ' ' | Where-Object { $_ }); $best = & $wn.HeadW1 $C
  for ($i = 1; $i -lt $words.Count; $i++) {
    $a = & $wn.TextW (($words[0..($i - 1)]) -join ' ') $ui.F.SmallB; $b = & $wn.TextW (($words[$i..($words.Count - 1)]) -join ' ') $ui.F.SmallB
    $best = [math]::Min($best, [math]::Max($a, $b)) }
  return $best }
# R11 (R38): the width column $C needs for its widest value in $Rows: the text as the grid paints it (a chip: the text and
# the chip's own padding, as $wn.PaintChip draws it) plus the cell padding at both sides and 1 px (right of a chip: at least
# the width of a vertical scroll bar, so the chip never ends under it); 0 when no row has a value.
$wn.ValueMin = { param($C, $Rows)
  $f = $(if ($C.K -eq 'with' -or $C.K -eq 'bold' -or $C.K -eq 'chip') { $ui.F.SmallB } else { $ui.F.Small }); $w = 0
  foreach ($r in @($Rows)) { $t = & $wn.CellText $C $r; if ($t) { $w = [math]::Max($w, (& $wn.TextW $t $f)) } }
  if ($w -le 0) { return 0 }
  # a chip: its text, its own padding, the cell padding left and, right of it, at least a scroll bar's width
  if ($C.K -eq 'chip') { return ($w + (& $ui.Sc 20) + (& $ui.Sc 10) + [math]::Max((& $ui.Sc 10), [int](& $wn.BarW)) + 1) }
  return ($w + 2 * (& $ui.Sc 10) + 1) }
$wn.GridEdges = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  R11 (R38): where the content of a grid's cells ends, against the room before its vertical scroll bar.
  .DESCRIPTION
  For each visible column, from the left: a chip column ends at its cell's left, the cell padding and its widest chip; the
  last visible column of another kind at its left, the padding and the widest value (never past the cell less its
  padding); the other columns end inside the grid and are not measured. Edge is the largest of these. Bar is the width of a vertical scroll bar, always reserved (the bar shows or not).
  .PARAMETER G
  The grid ($wn.Grid).
  .OUTPUTS
  @{ Grid; Width (the client width); Bar; Edge; Col (the column that reaches it); Fits (R11: the grid has no chip column, or
  $wn.GridCols kept its chip whole (Tag.ChipKept); when it did not, the heads come first and the edge is not judged) }.
  #>
  param($G)
  $pd = & $ui.Sc 10; $left = 0; $edge = 0; $name = ''; $cols = @($G.Tag.Cols)
  $shown = @($G.Columns | Sort-Object DisplayIndex | Where-Object { $_.Visible }); $lastName = $(if ($shown.Count) { [string]$shown[-1].Name } else { '' })
  foreach ($k in $shown) {
    $c = @($cols | Where-Object { [string]$_.N -eq $k.Name }) | Select-Object -First 1
    if ($c.K -ne 'chip' -and [string]$k.Name -ne $lastName) { $left += $k.Width; continue }
    $f = $(if ($c.K -eq 'with' -or $c.K -eq 'bold' -or $c.K -eq 'chip') { $ui.F.SmallB } else { $ui.F.Small }); $w = 0
    foreach ($r in @($G.Tag.Shown)) { $w = [math]::Max($w, (& $wn.TextW (& $wn.CellText $c $r) $f)) }
    if ($c.K -eq 'chip') { if ($w -gt 0) { $w += & $ui.Sc 20 } }
    elseif ($c.K -eq 'pub') { $w = 0 }   # the pub column is checked by its own cut test (W1)
    $e = $left + $pd + $(if ($c.K -eq 'chip') { $w } else { [math]::Min($w, [math]::Max(0, $k.Width - 2 * $pd)) })
    if ($w -gt 0 -and $e -gt $edge) { $edge = $e; $name = [string]$k.Name }
    $left += $k.Width }
  $bar = [int](& $wn.BarW); $wd = [int]$G.ClientSize.Width
  return @{ Grid = [string]$G.AccessibleName; Width = $wd; Bar = $bar; Edge = [int]$edge; Col = $name; Fits = ($null -eq $G.Tag.ChipKept -or [bool]$G.Tag.ChipKept) } }
# R11 (R38): the LAYOUT line of grid $G when a chip or text ends closer than the scroll bar's width to the grid's right
# edge (none when it does not).
$wn.EdgeCheck = { param($G, [string]$Card)
  $e = & $wn.GridEdges $G
  if (-not $e.Fits) {   # too narrow for every head and the whole chip: the heads come first (Test-EdgeBar prints INFO); R15: but
    $sb = [int](& $wn.BarShown $G); $s = 0; foreach ($k in @($G.Columns)) { if ($k.Visible) { $s += [int]$k.Width } }   # never under a bar that shows
    if ($sb -gt 0 -and $s -gt $e.Width - $sb) { return ('LAYOUT ' + $Card + ' R15 grid ' + $e.Grid + ': the columns end at ' + $s + ', the grid is ' + $e.Width +
        ' wide with a scroll bar of ' + $sb + ' showing') }
    return $null }
  if ($e.Edge -gt $e.Width - $e.Bar) {
    return ('LAYOUT ' + $Card + ' R11 grid ' + $e.Grid + ': column ' + $e.Col + ' ends at ' + $e.Edge + ', the grid is ' + $e.Width + ' wide with a scroll bar of ' + $e.Bar) }
  return $null }
# R7 (W1): the height of one line of a pub cell, in pixels: the larger of the link font's height and its card line height.
$wn.PubLineH = { return [math]::Max([int]$ui.F.Link.Height, (& $wn.LineH $ui.F.Link)) }
# R7 (W1): the smallest width of the pub column of $Cols: its widest number, widest title ($Pw, $wn.PubWidths) or head,
# whichever is widest, plus the cell padding at both sides and 1 px; 0 when the grid has no pub column.
$wn.PubMin = { param($Cols, $Pw)
  $c = @($Cols | Where-Object { $_.K -eq 'pub' }) | Select-Object -First 1; if (-not $c) { return 0 }
  $hw = & $wn.TextW (& $wn.HeadText $c) $ui.F.SmallB
  return ([math]::Max([math]::Max([int]$Pw.Num, [int]$Pw.Title), $hw) + 2 * (& $ui.Sc 10) + 1) }
$wn.PaintPub = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  Paints a pub cell: the number as a link and the title in the grid's title column, or under the number when the
  widest title of the grid does not fit in that column.
  .DESCRIPTION
  R6 (R31b D4): the title column starts after the grid's widest number and its gap (Tag.PubW, Tag.PubGap), so every
  title starts at one x; the choice beside or under is made once for the grid (Tag.PubT, the widest title), so a long
  title is never cut and the titles never start at two places. What was drawn goes into Tag.Drawn[row], relative to
  the text rectangle: the right end of the number, the title's x, the number's bottom and the title's top.
  R7 (R32 W1): also what each text needs and what it was given (number and title width, the height of the lines and
  of the cell), so the measure part and the layout self-check find a cut cell. A line is $wn.PubLineH high.
  .PARAMETER Gr
  The graphics of the cell.
  .PARAMETER Text
  The cell value, "number|title".
  .PARAMETER Tr
  The text rectangle of the cell (inside its padding).
  .PARAMETER Fl
  The one-line text flags.
  .PARAMETER Fw
  The wrapping text flags.
  .PARAMETER Tag
  The grid's Tag: PubW, PubT, PubGap and Drawn.
  .PARAMETER Row
  The row index (the key in Tag.Drawn).
  #>
  param($Gr, [string]$Text, $Tr, $Fl, $Fw, $Tag, [int]$Row)
  $pp = $Text.Split('|')
  $w1 = & $wn.TextW $pp[0] $ui.F.Link; $lh = & $wn.PubLineH
  $col = [int]$Tag.PubW + [int]$Tag.PubGap                 # the title column, from the left of the text rectangle
  $beside = ($pp.Count -lt 2 -or [int]$Tag.PubT -le $Tr.Width - $col)
  if ($beside) {
    [Windows.Forms.TextRenderer]::DrawText($Gr, $pp[0], $ui.F.Link, $Tr, $pc.primary, $Fl)
    $tx = $col; $ty = 0; $nb = 0; $th = $lh; $tw = $Tr.Width - $col   # one line: the title's x is the column; top and bottom are not compared
    $rest = New-Object System.Drawing.Rectangle(($Tr.X + $col), $Tr.Y, ($Tr.Width - $col), $Tr.Height)
    if ($pp.Count -gt 1) { [Windows.Forms.TextRenderer]::DrawText($Gr, $pp[1], $ui.F.Small, $rest, $pc.muted, $Fl) } }
  else {   # the widest title does not fit in the column: every title goes on a second line (the row is 2 lines high, $wn.GridHeight)
    $ny = [int](($Tr.Height - 2 * $lh) / 2); $tx = 0; $ty = $ny + $lh; $nb = $ny + $lh; $th = 2 * $lh; $tw = $Tr.Width
    [Windows.Forms.TextRenderer]::DrawText($Gr, $pp[0], $ui.F.Link, (New-Object System.Drawing.Rectangle($Tr.X, ($Tr.Y + $ny), $Tr.Width, $lh)), $pc.primary, $Fl)
    [Windows.Forms.TextRenderer]::DrawText($Gr, $pp[1], $ui.F.Small, (New-Object System.Drawing.Rectangle($Tr.X, ($Tr.Y + $ty), $Tr.Width, $lh)), $pc.muted, $Fw) }
  if ($null -eq $Tag.Drawn -or $pp.Count -lt 2) { return }
  $Tag.Drawn[$Row] = @{ NumRight = [math]::Min($w1, $Tr.Width); TitleX = $tx; NumBottom = $nb; TitleTop = $ty; Beside = $beside
    NumW = $w1; NumHave = $Tr.Width; TitleW = (& $wn.TextW $pp[1] $ui.F.Small); TitleHave = $tw; NeedH = $th; HaveH = $Tr.Height } }
# Paints a status chip cell: a rounded fill of the row's chip kind with the status in the middle. $Bd: the cell bounds; $Pd: its padding.
$wn.PaintChip = { param($Gr, [string]$Text, [string]$Kind, $Bd, [int]$Pd)
  $cwid = [Windows.Forms.TextRenderer]::MeasureText($Text, $ui.F.SmallB, ([Drawing.Size]::new(100000, 0)), [Windows.Forms.TextFormatFlags]'NoPadding, NoPrefix').Width + (& $ui.Sc 20)
  $chh = & $ui.Sc 26; $cy = $Bd.Y + [int](($Bd.Height - 1 - $chh) / 2); $rc = New-Object System.Drawing.RectangleF(($Bd.X + $Pd), $cy, $cwid, $chh)
  $Gr.SmoothingMode = 'AntiAlias'; $path = Get-PfmRoundPath $rc ($chh / 2.0); $br = New-Object System.Drawing.SolidBrush($wn.Fills[$Kind]); $Gr.FillPath($br, $path); $br.Dispose(); $path.Dispose()
  $Gr.SmoothingMode = 'Default'
  $tf = [Windows.Forms.TextFormatFlags]'HorizontalCenter, VerticalCenter, SingleLine, NoPadding, NoPrefix'
  [Windows.Forms.TextRenderer]::DrawText($Gr, $Text, $ui.F.SmallB, (New-Object System.Drawing.Rectangle(($Bd.X + $Pd), $cy, [int]$cwid, $chh)), $pc.ink, $tf) }
$wn.PaintCell = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  Paints one grid cell (the CellPainting event): the header in muted capitals with a line under it, or a row cell by its column kind.
  .PARAMETER S
  The grid.
  .PARAMETER E
  The event arguments (cell bounds, graphics, value; Handled is set).
  #>
  param($S, $E)
  try {
    $tag = $S.Tag; $kind = [string]$tag.Kind[$S.Columns[$E.ColumnIndex].Name]; $bd = $E.CellBounds; $gr = $E.Graphics; $pd = & $ui.Sc 10
    $fl = [Windows.Forms.TextFormatFlags]'Left, VerticalCenter, SingleLine, NoPadding, NoPrefix, EndEllipsis'
    $fw = [Windows.Forms.TextFormatFlags]'Left, VerticalCenter, WordBreak, NoPadding, NoPrefix'
    $tr = New-Object System.Drawing.Rectangle(($bd.X + $pd), $bd.Y, [math]::Max(1, $bd.Width - 2 * $pd), ($bd.Height - 1))
    $head = ($E.RowIndex -lt 0)
    $bg = $(if (-not $head -and $S.Rows[$E.RowIndex].Selected) { $pc.surface } else { $ui.C.White })
    $br = New-Object System.Drawing.SolidBrush($bg); $gr.FillRectangle($br, $bd); $br.Dispose()
    $pn = New-Object System.Drawing.Pen($(if ($head) { $pc.muted } else { $pc.line }), 1); $gr.DrawLine($pn, $bd.X, ($bd.Bottom - 1), $bd.Right, ($bd.Bottom - 1)); $pn.Dispose()
    $text = [string]$E.Value
    if ($head) {
      $cd = @(@($tag.Cols) | Where-Object { [string]$_.N -eq [string]$S.Columns[$E.ColumnIndex].Name }) | Select-Object -First 1
      $wrapHead = [bool]($cd -and $cd.HW)   # R11: a head that wraps to 2 lines (WordBreak) and needs the width of its wider line
      [Windows.Forms.TextRenderer]::DrawText($gr, $text.ToUpperInvariant(), $ui.F.SmallB, $tr, $pc.muted, $(if ($wrapHead) { $fw } else { $fl }))
      # R7 (W1): what the head of the pub column needs and has, for the measure part and the layout self-check
      $hd = @{ Text = $text.ToUpperInvariant(); W = $(if ($wrapHead) { (& $wn.HeadWrap $cd) } else { (& $wn.TextW $text.ToUpperInvariant() $ui.F.SmallB) }); Have = $tr.Width; Kind = $kind }
      if ($kind -eq 'pub') { $tag.Head = $hd }
      if ($null -ne $tag.Heads) { $tag.Heads[[string]$S.Columns[$E.ColumnIndex].Name] = $hd } }   # R8 (W7): every head, for the same checks
    elseif ($kind -eq 'pub') { & $wn.PaintPub $gr $text $tr $fl $fw $tag $E.RowIndex }
    elseif ($kind -eq 'with') { [Windows.Forms.TextRenderer]::DrawText($gr, $text, $ui.F.SmallB, $tr, $pc.navy, $fw) }
    elseif ($kind -eq 'bold') { [Windows.Forms.TextRenderer]::DrawText($gr, $text, $ui.F.SmallB, $tr, $pc.ink, $fw) }
    elseif ($kind -eq 'chip') { & $wn.PaintChip $gr $text ([string]$tag.Chip[$text]) $bd $pd }
    else { [Windows.Forms.TextRenderer]::DrawText($gr, $text, $ui.F.Small, $tr, $ui.C.Ink, $fw) }
    $E.Handled = $true
  } catch { $null = $_ } }
# Opens the card of grid row $I after the current event has ended (a card change inside a grid event would dispose the grid in its own handler).
$wn.Later = { param($G, [int]$I) $wn.PendG = $G; $wn.PendI = $I; [void]$form.BeginInvoke([Action]{ & $wn.OpenRow $wn.PendG $wn.PendI }) }
# Opens the card that grid row $I goes to, as its Open button would.
$wn.OpenRow = { param($G, [int]$I)
  $r = @($G.Tag.Shown)[$I]
  if ($r -and $r.Go) { & $wn.Press @{ Go = [string]$r.Go; Text = 'Open' } } }
# Filters the All Actions grid by the search text and the "Show" choice, and updates its count line.
$wn.Refilter = {
  $g = $wn.Gridq; if (-not $g) { return }
  $q = ([string]$wn.Field.find).Trim(); $m = [int]$wn.Field.show
  $rows = @($GridQueue | Where-Object { ($m -eq 0 -or ($m -eq 1 -and $_.Me) -or ($m -eq 2 -and $_.Kind -eq 'late')) -and
      (-not $q -or ([string]$_.Publication).IndexOf($q, [System.StringComparison]::OrdinalIgnoreCase) -ge 0) })
  & $wn.GridFill $g $rows; $g.ClearSelection()
  if ($wn.CountBox) { $wn.CountBox.Text = ([string]$wn.CountText -f $rows.Count) } }
'@ }

# <<< app-logo
# R8 (R35 W7): the 2 system colors of the logo with high contrast on: the dark disc and Z take Window, the light rings,
# page and arc take WindowText (the rail behind it is WindowText, so the disc stands out from the rail).
$wn.LogoRole = @{ Dark = 'Window'; Light = 'WindowText' }
# R10 (R37; PFM 19 Nov 26: the logo rule of the bookmark page): whether Windows apps use light mode: $true when the
# value AppsUseLightTheme under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Themes\Personalize is 1 or missing
# (also when it cannot be read), $false when it is 0. Read only; nothing is written.
$wn.AppsLight = {
  try { $v = Get-ItemProperty -LiteralPath 'HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Themes\Personalize' -Name 'AppsUseLightTheme' -ErrorAction Stop
    return ([int]$v.AppsUseLightTheme -ne 0) } catch { return $true } }
# R11 (R38; PFM 20 Nov 26): the logo in its own colors: the Fulcrum logo ($AppLogoPng, the app-logo block), in Windows light
# and dark mode alike.
$wn.LogoOwn = {
  return [Drawing.Image]::FromStream((New-Object System.IO.MemoryStream(, [System.Convert]::FromBase64String($AppLogoPng)))) }
# R8 (R35 W7): the logo picture for high contrast $High: its own colors when off (R11: the Fulcrum logo, $wn.LogoOwn);
# when on, a copy of it in the 2 system colors of $wn.LogoRole (ConvertTo-PfmTwoTone; each pixel keeps its cover), as in r8.
$wn.LogoImage = { param([bool]$High)
  if (-not $High) { return (& $wn.LogoOwn) }
  $img = & $wn.LogoOwn
  $d = [string]$wn.LogoRole.Dark; $l = [string]$wn.LogoRole.Light
  try { return (ConvertTo-PfmTwoTone $img ([Drawing.SystemColors]::$d) ([Drawing.SystemColors]::$l)) } finally { $img.Dispose() } }
$wn.MeasureTheme = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  R11 (R38): the one own-color logo (Fulcrum, in Windows light and dark mode), and the app mode of this computer, with no
  change of the Windows setting.
  .OUTPUTS
  A table: Light (the app mode read here), Fulcrum (its size) and ShownDiff (the rail logo against the Fulcrum logo; 0 =
  the right one, -1 when no rail logo is shown or high contrast is on).
  #>
  $f = [ordered]@{}; $f['Light'] = [bool](& $wn.AppsLight)
  $fu = & $wn.LogoOwn
  try { $f['Fulcrum'] = ([string]$fu.Width + 'x' + $fu.Height)
    $f['ShownDiff'] = $(if ($wn.Logo -and $wn.Logo.Image -and -not $ui.High) { (Get-PfmPixelDiff $wn.Logo.Image $fu) } else { -1 }) }
  finally { $fu.Dispose() }
  return $f }
'@ }

$wn.Press = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  What a card button, link or grid row does: checks what it needs, keeps its note, then opens the card it goes to.
  .DESCRIPTION
  A click in the first moments after a card changed does nothing ($ui.Settled). Need = reason: the reason box must have
  text; Need = ck: both boxes must be selected; else the card shows its error line. Go: a card key, 'back', or '@grid'
  (the selected row of the card's grid); no Go shows the same card again with the button's FAKE note.
  .PARAMETER B
  The button table: Text, Go, Note, Need.
  #>
  param($B)
  if (-not (& $ui.Settled)) { & $wn.IgnoreNote ('the button ' + [string]$B.Text); return }   # R16: a dropped click leaves a NOTE line (bar part)
  $script:presses++
  $need = [string]$B.Need
  if ($need -eq 'reason' -and -not ([string]$wn.Field.reason).Trim()) { $wn.Err = 'reason'; $wn.Notice = ''; $wn.Focus = 'reason'; & $wn.Show $wn.Cur; return }
  if ($need -eq 'ck' -and -not ($wn.Field.ck1 -and $wn.Field.ck2)) { $wn.Err = 'ck'; $wn.Notice = ''; & $wn.Show $wn.Cur; return }
  $wn.Err = ''; $wn.Notice = [string]$B.Note
  $go = [string]$B.Go
  if ($go -eq '@grid') {   # the selected row of the card's grid, else its first row
    $go = ''; $g = $wn.Gridsel
    if ($g -and @($g.Tag.Shown).Count) { $i = 0; if ($g.SelectedRows.Count) { $i = [int]$g.SelectedRows[0].Index }; $go = [string]@($g.Tag.Shown)[$i].Go } }
  if ($go -eq 'back') { $go = $wn.Prev }
  if (-not $go) { $go = $wn.Cur }
  try { & $wn.Show $go } catch { & $wn.OpenFail $go $_ }   # R15: a NOTE line when the open stops (bar part)
  & $wn.OpenCheck $go }   # R16: and when it returns with no error and the window stays on the old card
# The rail is wider when the window is wide; its items follow its width.
$wn.RailLayout = {
  $wide = ($form.ClientSize.Width -ge (& $wn.Sc 1500)); $rw = $(if ($wide) { & $wn.Sc 220 } else { & $wn.Sc 200 }); $rail.Width = $rw
  foreach ($x in $wn.RailBtn) { $x.Width = $rw - 2 * (& $wn.Sc 12) } }
$wn.HeadParts = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  Builds the logo and the app name "90-161.Z" of the rail head into $Into (R31 W1).
  .DESCRIPTION
  The logo (40 x 40 at 100 %, at 16,16) sits on the rail's navy, the same color as the name, so no white box shows
  behind it. The name is placed by its middle, not its top: its middle is the logo's middle (rounded to a pixel), at
  any scale. A logo that cannot be shown is a NOTE line, not an error; the name keeps its place. The measure part
  builds the same parts into a test panel at 1.5 x to measure the centering at a second scale.
  R8 (R35 W7): the logo picture follows the high-contrast setting ($wn.LogoImage $ui.High).
  .PARAMETER Into
  The panel the parts go into (the rail).
  .PARAMETER WordFont
  The font of the name (the RADE logo word, $ui.F.Word).
  .OUTPUTS
  @{ Logo (the picture box, or $null); Name (the label) }.
  #>
  param($Into, $WordFont)
  $out = @{ Logo = $null; Name = $null }; $top = & $wn.Sc 16; $side = & $wn.Sc 40
  try {
    $logo = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.PictureBox; $logo.Size = [Drawing.Size]::new($side, $side); $logo.SizeMode = 'Zoom'; $logo.BackColor = $pc.navy
    $logo.AccessibleName = '90-161.Z logo'; $logo.Location = [Drawing.Point]::new((& $wn.Sc 16), $top)
    $logo.Image = & $wn.LogoImage ([bool]$ui.High); [void]$Into.Controls.Add($logo); $out.Logo = $logo
  } catch { $lines.Add('NOTE logo not shown: ' + $_.Exception.Message) }
  $nm = & $ui.Label $WordFont $ui.C.White 0; $nm.BackColor = $pc.navy; $nm.Text = 'Kanon'; $nm.Visible = $true
  $nh = [int]$nm.PreferredSize.Height
  $nm.Location = [Drawing.Point]::new((& $wn.Sc 64), ($top + [int][math]::Round(($side - $nh) / 2.0)))
  [void]$Into.Controls.Add($nm); $out.Name = $nm
  return $out }
# The rail head: the logo and the app name ($wn.HeadParts; kept in $wn.Logo and $wn.AppName for the measure part) and the

  try { $lf = & $wn.LogoFacts; $bad = @(& $wn.LogoBad $lf); foreach ($x in $bad) { $ui.LayBad.Add([string]$x) }
    $own = 'high contrast off: own colors (Fulcrum, light and dark mode)'
    if ($lf.Shown) { $lines.Add('LOGO ' + $(if ($lf.High) { 'high contrast on: system colors' } else { $own }) + ', other pixels ' + $lf.Other +
        ', changed pixels ' + $lf.Diff + $(if ($bad.Count) { ' (wrong colors)' } else { ' (right colors)' })) } }
  catch { $lines.Add('NOTE the logo check stopped: ' + ([string]$_.Exception.Message)) }
  $sb = & $ui.Label $ui.F.Small $pc.onPrimaryMuted 0; $sb.BackColor = $pc.navy; $sb.Text = 'Publications and Forms'; $sb.Visible = $true
  $sb.Location = [Drawing.Point]::new((& $wn.Sc 16), (& $wn.Sc 66)); [void]$rail.Controls.Add($sb) }
$wn.BuildRail = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  Builds the rail: its head, one item per rail entry (Your Work has a badge) and the "FAKE data" line at the bottom.
  .DESCRIPTION
  A rail item opens its card (Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+5 do the same, $wn.Hook). Then the rail takes its width ($wn.RailLayout).
  #>
  $rail.SuspendLayout()
  & $wn.RailHead
  $y = & $wn.Sc 108
  foreach ($r in $RailItems) {
    $x = Build-PfmRailItem; $x.Text = $r.Text; $x.AccessibleName = $r.Text; $x.Tag = $r.Key; $x.Font = $ui.F.Body; $x.BoldFont = $ui.F.SmallB
    $x.Back = $pc.navy; $x.OnBack = $ui.C.White; $x.Fore = $pc.onPrimaryMuted; $x.OnFore = $pc.navy; $x.HotLine = $pc.onPrimaryMuted; $x.FocusLine = $pc.accentFill
    $x.FocusOn = $pc.navy; $x.BadgeFill = $pc.accentFill; $x.BadgeText = $pc.ink; $x.BackColor = $x.Back; $x.ForeColor = $x.Fore   # R11 (B10)
    if ($r.Badge) { $x.Badge = [string]$r.Badge; $x.AccessibleName = $r.Text + ', ' + $r.Badge + ' items need you' }
    $x.Size = [Drawing.Size]::new(((& $wn.Sc 200) - 2 * (& $wn.Sc 12)), (& $wn.Sc 44)); $x.Location = [Drawing.Point]::new((& $wn.Sc 12), $y); $y += (& $wn.Sc 48)
    # R16 (R42 finding 5: Reviews Due sometimes needed 2 clicks): the 400 ms guard after a card changed (it stops the second click of
    # a double-click) holds a rail click only when it opens the card that shows now; a click that opens another card is not held.
    $x.Add_Click({ $key = [string]$this.Tag; $go = 'home'; foreach ($q in $RailItems) { if ($q.Key -eq $key) { $go = $q.Go } }
        if (-not (& $ui.Settled) -and $go -eq $wn.Cur) { & $wn.IgnoreNote ('the list item ' + $this.Text); return }
        $script:presses++; $wn.Notice = ''; $wn.Err = ''
        try { & $wn.Show $go } catch { & $wn.OpenFail $go $_ }
        & $wn.OpenCheck $go })
    [void]$rail.Controls.Add($x); $wn.RailBtn += $x }
  $src = $(if ($script:SiteSource -eq 'site') { 'Test site data' } else { 'FAKE data' })   # R14: the source of the cards (site part)
  $ft = & $ui.Label $ui.F.Small $pc.onPrimaryMuted 0; $ft.BackColor = $pc.navy; $ft.Text = $src + [Environment]::NewLine + 'Preview ' + $Rev; $ft.Visible = $true; $ft.Anchor = 'Left, Bottom'
  $ft.Location = [Drawing.Point]::new((& $wn.Sc 16), ($rail.ClientSize.Height - (& $wn.Sc 56))); [void]$rail.Controls.Add($ft)
  $rail.ResumeLayout($true); & $wn.RailLayout }
$wn.Crumb = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  The crumb line of a card: its first part as a link, the rest as text, in one font and size (R30 V2).
  .DESCRIPTION
  The link is a Build-PfmLinkText button: the crumb's own font (the small text font) underlined, the link blue, no padding, so its
  size is its text. The rest starts with the arrow, a small gap after the link (3 px at 100 %, room for the focus ring),
  so the gap from the link's text to the arrow stays under 8 px at 100 %. A crumb with no link is one text.
  R6 (R31b D2): the link draws its text in its vertical middle; the rest's top gap is set so that the middle of its
  line is the link's middle (within half a pixel, at any scale), so both parts sit on one line.
  .PARAMETER C
  The card: Crumb, CrumbGo.
  .PARAMETER Cw
  The width of the page column.
  .OUTPUTS
  The text box of the crumb's rest (the card's title for the layout self-check).
  #>
  param($C, [int]$Cw)
  $cf = & $wn.Flow $page $pc.surface; $cf.Margin = & $ui.Pad 0 0 0 (& $wn.Sc 8)
  $parts = @(([string]$C.Crumb) -split [regex]::Escape(' ' + $gt + ' '))
  if (-not ($C.CrumbGo -and $parts.Count -gt 1)) { return (& $wn.Txt $cf $C.Crumb $ui.F.Small $ui.C.Gray 0 $Cw 'Where you are' $pc.surface) }
  $l = Build-PfmLinkText; $l.Text = $parts[0]; $l.Font = $wn.CrumbFont; $l.ForeColor = $ui.C.Blue; $l.BackColor = $pc.surface
  $l.AutoSize = $true; $l.AutoSizeMode = 'GrowAndShrink'
  $l.MinimumSize = [Drawing.Size]::new(0, (& $wn.Sc $ui.Z.LinkH)); Resize-PfmLinkText $l   # R21: the maximum size makes the preferred size the text's
  $l.Margin = & $ui.Pad (& $wn.Sc $ui.Z.M) (& $wn.Sc $ui.Z.M) 0 (& $wn.Sc $ui.Z.M)
  $l.AccessibleName = $parts[0]; $l.AccessibleRole = 'Link'; $l.Tag = @{ Text = $parts[0]; Go = $C.CrumbGo }
  $l.Add_Click({ & $wn.Press $this.Tag }); & $ui.Cue $l; [void]$cf.Controls.Add($l); $wn.CrumbLink = $l
  $rest = $gt + ' ' + ((@($parts | Select-Object -Skip 1)) -join (' ' + $gt + ' '))
  $t = & $wn.Txt $cf $rest $ui.F.Small $ui.C.Gray 8 ($Cw - (& $wn.Sc 160)) 'Where you are' $pc.surface
  # The link's middle from the row top: its top gap and half its height (its preferred height, as the flow sizes it).
  $mid = $l.Margin.Top + $l.GetPreferredSize([Drawing.Size]::Empty).Height / 2.0
  $top = [int][math]::Max(0, [math]::Round($mid - (& $wn.LineH $t.Font) / 2.0))
  $t.Margin = & $ui.Pad (& $wn.Sc 3) $top 0 0; $wn.CrumbRest = $t
  return $t }
# The FAKE note of the last button: the NOTICE chip and the note beside it, the chip level with the note's first line
# (R7 W3, $wn.ChipTops). $Cw: the width of the page column.
$wn.ShowNotice = { param([int]$Cw)
  $nf = & $wn.Flow $page $pc.surface; $nf.Margin = & $ui.Pad 0 0 0 (& $wn.Sc 10); $cp = & $wn.Chip 'turn' 'NOTICE' $pc.surface; [void]$nf.Controls.Add($cp)
  $nt = & $wn.Txt $nf $wn.Notice $ui.F.Body $ui.C.Ink 0 ($Cw - (& $wn.Sc 120)) 'Notice' $pc.surface
  $tops = & $wn.ChipTops $cp.Height $nt.Font 0; $nt.Margin = & $ui.Pad 0 $tops.Text 0 0; $cp.Margin = & $ui.Pad 0 $tops.Chip $cp.Margin.Right 0
  & $wn.KeepChip $cp $nt 'notice' }
# The head of a card: the FAKE note of the last button, the crumb, the title and the line under it. Sets $ui.Sent and
# $ui.Kick (the title and the line the layout self-check reads).
$wn.ShowHead = { param($C, [int]$Cw)
  $title = $null
  if ($wn.Notice) { & $wn.ShowNotice $Cw }
  if ($C.Crumb) { $title = & $wn.Crumb $C $Cw }
  if ($C.Title) { $title = & $wn.Txt $page $C.Title $ui.F.Sent $ui.C.Navy 0 $Cw 'Page title' $pc.surface }
  if ($C.Sub) { $ui.Kick = & $wn.Txt $page $C.Sub $ui.F.Small $ui.C.Gray 4 $Cw 'Page line' $pc.surface } else { $ui.Kick = $title }
  $ui.Sent = $title }
$wn.ShowCols = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  The columns of a card: one column, or a main column and a side column; each section is a card with its blocks.
  .DESCRIPTION
  Each section built is kept in $wn.Secs (column number, card, caption, Stretch, caption box) for $wn.LevelCaps,
  $wn.Align and the measure part.
  .PARAMETER C
  The card data.
  .PARAMETER Key
  The card key (Your Work has a wider side column).
  .PARAMETER Cw
  The width of the page column.
  .PARAMETER Wide
  True when the window is wide (WideOnly sections show, the side column of Your Work is wider).
  #>
  param($C, [string]$Key, [int]$Cw, [bool]$Wide)
  $cols = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.FlowLayoutPanel; $cols.FlowDirection = 'LeftToRight'; $cols.WrapContents = $false; $cols.AutoSize = $true; $cols.AutoSizeMode = 'GrowAndShrink'
  $cols.BackColor = $pc.surface; $cols.Margin = & $ui.Pad 0 (& $wn.Sc 12) 0 0; [void]$page.Controls.Add($cols)
  $gap = & $wn.Sc 18; $nc = @($C.Cols).Count
  $side = $(if ($nc -gt 1) { $(if ($Key -eq 'home' -or $Key -eq 'empty') { $(if ($Wide) { & $wn.Sc 420 } else { & $wn.Sc 300 }) } else { & $wn.Sc $C.Side }) } else { 0 })
  $ci = 0
  foreach ($colDef in @($C.Cols)) {
    $colW = $(if ($nc -le 1) { [math]::Min($Cw, (& $wn.Sc 1000)) } elseif ($ci -eq 0) { $Cw - $side - $gap } else { $side })
    $col = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.FlowLayoutPanel; $col.FlowDirection = 'TopDown'; $col.WrapContents = $false; $col.AutoSize = $true; $col.AutoSizeMode = 'GrowAndShrink'
    $col.BackColor = $pc.surface; $col.Margin = & $ui.Pad 0 0 $(if ($ci -eq 0 -and $nc -gt 1) { $gap } else { 0 }) 0; [void]$cols.Controls.Add($col)
    $ctx = @{ Col = $col }
    foreach ($s in @($colDef)) {
      if ($s.WideOnly -and -not $Wide) { continue }
      $px = $(if ($s.Pad) { [int]$s.Pad } else { 24 })
      $sec = & $wn.Card $colW $s.Cap $s.Top $px $pc.surface; [void]$col.Controls.Add($sec)
      # CapBox: the caption text box, the card's first child when it has a caption ($wn.Card adds it first).
      $wn.Secs += @{ Col = $ci; Card = $sec; Cap = [string]$s.Cap; Stretch = [bool]$s.Stretch; CapBox = $(if ($s.Cap) { $sec.Controls[0] } else { $null }) }
      $iw = $colW - 2 * (& $wn.Sc $px)
      foreach ($b in @($s.Blocks)) { & $wn.Block $sec $b $iw $ctx }
      $sec.PerformLayout() }
    $ci++ } }
# The first line of text of a section card: the first card text box in the order its parts were added, looking inside
# a row (the chips row holds the step line). Gives back the text box, or $null.
$wn.FirstLine = { param($Sec)
  foreach ($c in $Sec.Controls) {
    if (& $ui.IsCardText $c) { return $c }
    if ($c.Controls.Count) { $in = & $wn.FirstLine $c; if ($in) { return $in } } }
  return $null }
$wn.LevelCaps = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  R6 (R31b D1): the caption of each Action Status card (Stretch) is level with the first line of the main card beside it.
  .DESCRIPTION
  The columns start at one top, so the two middles compare directly ($wn.TextMid, page pixels). The higher of the two
  moves down by the difference, rounded to a pixel: the caption by its top gap, or (when the caption is the lower one)
  the main card's first part. Then the page lays out again; $wn.Align runs after this and lines up the bottoms.
  #>
  $mainSec = @($wn.Secs | Where-Object { $_.Col -eq 0 }) | Select-Object -First 1
  if (-not $mainSec) { return }
  $line = & $wn.FirstLine $mainSec.Card; if (-not $line) { return }
  $moved = $false
  foreach ($s in @($wn.Secs | Where-Object { $_.Stretch -and $_.CapBox })) {
    $d = [int][math]::Round((& $wn.TextMid $line) - (& $wn.TextMid $s.CapBox))
    if ($d -eq 0) { continue }
    $mv = $(if ($d -gt 0) { $s.CapBox } else { $mainSec.Card.Controls[0] })
    $m = $mv.Margin; $mv.Margin = & $ui.Pad $m.Left ($m.Top + [math]::Abs($d)) $m.Right $m.Bottom
    $s.Card.PerformLayout(); $mainSec.Card.PerformLayout(); $moved = $true }
  if ($moved) { $page.PerformLayout() } }
# R30 V4: in a card with an Action Status card (Stretch), the last cards of the columns end on one line: the shorter one
# grows to the bottom of the longer one. The columns start at one top, so their bottoms compare directly.
$wn.Align = {
  if (-not @($wn.Secs | Where-Object { $_.Stretch }).Count) { return }
  $last = @{}; foreach ($s in $wn.Secs) { $last[$s.Col] = $s }
  if ($last.Count -lt 2) { return }
  $low = 0; foreach ($s in $last.Values) { $low = [math]::Max($low, $s.Card.Parent.Top + $s.Card.Bottom) }
  foreach ($s in $last.Values) { $d = $low - ($s.Card.Parent.Top + $s.Card.Bottom); if ($d -gt 0) { $s.Card.MinimumSize = [Drawing.Size]::new($s.Card.MinimumSize.Width, $s.Card.Height + $d) } }
  $page.PerformLayout() }
$wn.ShowBuild = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  Builds card $Key on a new page: the head and the columns, the side captions level (D1), the column bottoms in line.
  .DESCRIPTION
  R13 (R40): the card goes on its own new page ($wn.NewPage, keep part), which replaces the page shown; the old kept
  page of this card, if any, goes first ($wn.KeepDrop). The new page is kept ($wn.KeepSave) for the next open.
  .PARAMETER C
  The card data.
  .PARAMETER Key
  The card key.
  .PARAMETER Cw
  The width of the page column.
  .PARAMETER Sig
  What the card is built for ($wn.KeepSig).
  #>
  param($C, [string]$Key, [int]$Cw, [string]$Sig)
  $wn.Primary = $null; $wn.Gridsel = $null; $wn.Gridq = $null; $wn.Reason = $null; $wn.CountBox = $null; $wn.CrumbLink = $null; $wn.CrumbRest = $null; $wn.Secs = @(); $wn.ChipRows = @()
  $ui.Wrap = @{}; $ui.Boxes = @()
  & $wn.KeepDrop $Key
  & $wn.PageSwap (& $wn.NewPage)
  $page.SuspendLayout()
  $page.Location = [Drawing.Point]::new($wn.PadX, (& $wn.Sc 22)); $page.Margin = & $ui.Pad 0 0 0 0; $page.Padding = & $ui.Pad 0 0 0 (& $wn.Sc 22)
  & $wn.ShowHead $C $Cw
  $page.PerformLayout(); $wn.HeadH = [int]$page.PreferredSize.Height
  & $wn.ShowCols $C $Key $Cw $wn.Wide
  $page.ResumeLayout($true); $form.ResumeLayout($true)
  & $wn.LevelCaps; & $wn.Align
  $null = & $wn.FitGrids   # R10 (R37): a grid whose columns are wider than it gives the excess back
  & $wn.KeepSave $Key $Sig }
$wn.Show = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  Shows the card $Key: its kept page when that was built for this size, note and error line, else a new build.
  .DESCRIPTION
  A new card forgets the fields of the last one (a modal card remembers the card to go back to). The main button gets
  the focus (or the reason box after an empty reason) and the Enter key. The layout self-check runs a moment later.
  R13 (R40, R39 finding 2): the card already shown is always built again (a note, an error line, a resize); another
  card shows its kept page when $wn.KeepFind has one (no control is built: the open is a hide and a show), else it is
  built ($wn.ShowBuild). The rules: the keep part's header. The page column width comes from the main column's full
  width, with or without its scroll bar, so it does not depend on the card shown before (r12 measured the width that
  was left beside the last card's scroll bar).
  R14 (R41; R40 finding 3): $wn.OpenKind names the open (first, kept, rebuild, resize) for the layout self-check line.
  .PARAMETER Key
  The card key in $Cards; an unknown key does nothing.
  #>
  param([string]$Key)
  $c = $Cards[$Key]; if (-not $c) { $lines.Add('NOTE the screen ' + $Key + ' did not open: no such screen in the window'); return }   # R16: no silent return
  $t0 = $ui.Clock.Elapsed.TotalMilliseconds   # R12 (R38 finding 3): the open time of a card the person opens
  $again = ($Key -eq $wn.Cur)
  if (-not $again) { & $wn.KeepLeave; if ($c.Modal) { $wn.Prev = $wn.Cur }; $wn.Field = @{}; $wn.Err = ''; $wn.Focus = '' }
  $script:cardsOpened[$Key] = $true; $wn.Cur = $Key; $ui.View = $Key
  $ui.Hot = $null; $ui.Down = $null
  # R7 (W2): the main column goes back to its top first, so the page is placed in unscrolled pixels (placed while the
  # column was scrolled, the page kept that offset and the new card started lower, with empty space above it).
  $main.AutoScrollPosition = [Drawing.Point]::new(0, 0)
  $form.SuspendLayout()
  $wide = ($form.ClientSize.Width -ge (& $wn.Sc 1500)); $wn.Wide = $wide
  $wn.MainH = $main.ClientSize.Height; $padX = & $wn.Sc 28; $wn.PadX = $padX
  $cw = [math]::Max((& $wn.Sc 900), $main.Width - [Windows.Forms.SystemInformation]::VerticalScrollBarWidth - 2 * $padX)
  # R11 (UI standard v1, B10): ForeColor and BackColor hold the painted colors, so the contrast rule reads what shows
  foreach ($r in $wn.RailBtn) { $r.On = ([string]$r.Tag -eq [string]$c.Rail)
    $r.BackColor = $(if ($r.On) { $r.OnBack } else { $r.Back }); $r.ForeColor = $(if ($r.On) { $r.OnFore } else { $r.Fore }); $r.Invalidate() }
  $sig = & $wn.KeepSig $cw
  $kept = $(if ($again) { $null } else { & $wn.KeepFind $Key $sig }); $wn.KeepUsed = [bool]$kept
  # R14 (R41; R40 finding 3): which open this is, for the layout self-check line (first, kept, rebuild, resize)
  $wn.OpenKind = $(if ($wn.Resizing) { 'resize' } elseif ($kept) { 'kept' } elseif ($again -or $wn.Kept[$Key]) { 'rebuild' } else { 'first' }); $wn.FitTries = 0
  if ($kept) {   # R13: the kept page: its state back, the page shown in place of the last one, at the top, grids reset
    & $wn.KeepLoad $kept; & $wn.PageSwap $kept.Page
    $page.Location = [Drawing.Point]::new($padX, (& $wn.Sc 22)); & $wn.KeepReset $kept
    $form.ResumeLayout($true) }
  else { & $wn.ShowBuild $c $Key $cw $sig }
  $main.AutoScrollPosition = [Drawing.Point]::new(0, 0)
  $form.AcceptButton = $wn.Primary
  $ui.CardAt = $ui.Clock.Elapsed.TotalMilliseconds
  if ($wn.Focus -eq 'reason' -and $wn.Reason) { [void]$wn.Reason.Focus(); $wn.Focus = '' } elseif ($wn.Primary) { [void]$wn.Primary.Focus() }
  if ($wn.Ready) { $wn.CheckTimer.Stop(); $wn.CheckTimer.Start(); & $wn.KeepTime $Key $t0; & $wn.WalkSeen $Key } }   # R14: the click-through notes the open
# Where the window place is kept between runs (none with -Measure: no task folder).
# r21 (F6): new file name, so a place saved by r20 (DPI aware, physical pixels) is not read as logical pixels now.
$wn.BoundsFile = $(if ($dir) { Join-Path $dir '90161Z-T22-window-bounds-r21.json' } else { '' })
# R12 (R39; docs/phases.md): the card the window was closed on, opened again at the next start (none with -Measure).
$wn.LastFile = $(if ($dir) { Join-Path $dir '90161Z-T22-window-lastcard.txt' } else { '' })
# R13 (R40): the card key saved at the last close, or '' when there is none ($wn.OpenLast; the -Again check names it).
$wn.LastKey = {
  try { if ($wn.LastFile -and (Test-Path -LiteralPath $wn.LastFile -PathType Leaf)) { return ([string](Get-Content -LiteralPath $wn.LastFile -TotalCount 1)).Trim() } } catch { $null = $_ }
  return '' }
$wn.SaveLast = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  R12: saves the card the window shows at its close (for a modal card, the card it came from) for the next start.
  #>
  try {
    if (-not $wn.LastFile) { return }
    $k = $(if ($Cards[$wn.Cur] -and $Cards[$wn.Cur].Modal) { [string]$wn.Prev } else { [string]$wn.Cur })
    if ($Cards[$k]) { Set-Content -LiteralPath $wn.LastFile -Value $k -Encoding UTF8 }
  } catch { $lines.Add('NOTE the last card was not saved: ' + ([string]$_.Exception.Message)) } }
$wn.OpenLast = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  R12: shows the card saved at the last close, when it is a card that is not modal; else Your Work stays. Adds a
  LASTCARD line: the card opened, and where it came from.
  #>
  $k = & $wn.LastKey
  if ($k -and $Cards[$k] -and -not $Cards[$k].Modal) {
    if ($k -ne 'home') { $wn.Notice = ''; $wn.Err = ''; & $wn.Show $k }
    $lines.Add('LASTCARD opened=' + $k + ' (saved at the last close)') }
  else { $lines.Add('LASTCARD opened=home (' + $(if ($k) { 'saved card ' + $k + ' not used' } else { 'no saved card' }) + ')') } }
$wn.LoadBounds = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  Puts the window where it was last closed (if that place is on a screen and big enough), else at 90 % of the screen.
  #>
  $ok = $false
  try {
    if ($wn.BoundsFile -and (Test-Path -LiteralPath $wn.BoundsFile)) {
      $j = Get-Content -LiteralPath $wn.BoundsFile -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
      $r = New-Object System.Drawing.Rectangle([int]$j.Left, [int]$j.Top, [int]$j.Width, [int]$j.Height)
      $tl = [Drawing.Point]::new($r.X + (& $wn.Sc 40), $r.Y + (& $wn.Sc 10)); foreach ($sc in [Windows.Forms.Screen]::AllScreens) { if ($sc.WorkingArea.Contains($tl)) { $ok = $true } }
      if ($ok -and $r.Width -ge (& $wn.Sc 400) -and $r.Height -ge (& $wn.Sc 300)) {
        $form.StartPosition = 'Manual'; $form.Bounds = $r; if ([string]$j.State -eq 'Maximized') { $form.WindowState = 'Maximized' } } else { $ok = $false } }
  } catch { $ok = $false }
  if (-not $ok) {
    $wa = [Windows.Forms.Screen]::FromPoint([Windows.Forms.Cursor]::Position).WorkingArea
    $w = [int]($wa.Width * 0.9); $h = [int]($wa.Height * 0.9); $form.StartPosition = 'Manual'
    $form.Bounds = New-Object System.Drawing.Rectangle(($wa.X + [int](($wa.Width - $w) / 2)), ($wa.Y + [int](($wa.Height - $h) / 2)), $w, $h) } }
# Adds a STATE line (window state, client size, bounds) to the result.
$wn.State = { param([string]$When)
  $lines.Add('STATE ' + $When + ': WindowState=' + $form.WindowState + ' client=' + $form.ClientSize.Width + 'x' + $form.ClientSize.Height + ' bounds=' + $form.Bounds.Width + 'x' +
    $form.Bounds.Height + ' at ' + $form.Bounds.X + ',' + $form.Bounds.Y) }
# Saves the window's place and size (its normal bounds, and whether it was maximized) for the next run.
$wn.SaveBounds = {
  try {
    if (-not $wn.BoundsFile) { return }
    $r = $(if ($form.WindowState -eq 'Normal') { $form.Bounds } else { $form.RestoreBounds })
    $st = $(if ($form.WindowState -eq 'Maximized') { 'Maximized' } else { 'Normal' })
    $o = '{ "Left": ' + $r.X + ', "Top": ' + $r.Y + ', "Width": ' + $r.Width + ', "Height": ' + $r.Height + ', "State": "' + $st + '" }'
    Set-Content -LiteralPath $wn.BoundsFile -Value $o -Encoding UTF8
  } catch { $lines.Add('NOTE the window place was not saved: ' + ([string]$_.Exception.Message)) } }
# The check bar (the checks and, R14, the click-through) is in the bar part.
# The layout self-check runs 350 ms after a card changed; a new size rebuilds the card 250 ms after the last size change.
# R14 (R41; R40 finding 3, "columns need 811, the grid has 801" after a resize or a rebuild): when the grid fit of the
# tick changed a grid, the check waits one more tick for the layout to settle and fits again (at most 3 more ticks).
$wn.Ready = $false; $wn.LastW = 0; $wn.LastH = 0; $wn.OpenKind = 'first'; $wn.FitTries = 0; $wn.Resizing = $false
$wn.CheckTimer = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.Timer; $wn.CheckTimer.Interval = 350
$wn.CheckTimer.Add_Tick({ $wn.CheckTimer.Stop(); try {
      if ((& $wn.FitGrids) -gt 0 -and $wn.FitTries -lt 3) { $wn.FitTries++; $wn.CheckTimer.Start(); return }
      $wn.FitTries = 0; & $ui.Check; & $wn.ScrollCheck } catch { $null = $_ } })
# R14: fits the grids of the card on the page until a fit changes nothing (at most 3 fits, the layout settles between).
$wn.FitSettled = { for ($i = 0; $i -lt 3; $i++) { if (-not (& $wn.FitGrids)) { break }; [Windows.Forms.Application]::DoEvents() } }
$wn.SizeTimer = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.Timer; $wn.SizeTimer.Interval = 250
$wn.SizeTimer.Add_Tick({ $wn.SizeTimer.Stop()
    if ($form.ClientSize.Width -ne $wn.LastW -or $form.ClientSize.Height -ne $wn.LastH) {
      $wn.LastW = $form.ClientSize.Width; $wn.LastH = $form.ClientSize.Height; & $wn.RailLayout
      $wn.Resizing = $true; try { & $wn.Show $wn.Cur } finally { $wn.Resizing = $false } } })
$ui.Trash = @($ui.Trash) + @($wn.CheckTimer, $wn.SizeTimer)
# Grid columns wider than their grid, and a main column that scrolls sideways at 1280 or wider, are layout defects; a
# card whose main column scrolls down is noted in $wn.Scrolled.
$wn.ScrollCheck = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  The layout self-check of the card on the page: grids wider than themselves, the content of a grid ending closer to its
  right edge than a scroll bar is wide (R11), a main column that scrolls sideways at 1280 or wider.
  .DESCRIPTION
  Adds one LAYOUT line to $ui.LayBad for each defect; a card whose main column scrolls down is noted in $wn.Scrolled.
  .OUTPUTS
  None.
  #>
  $st = New-Object System.Collections.Stack; $st.Push($page)
  while ($st.Count) { foreach ($c in $st.Pop().Controls) {
      if ($c -is [Windows.Forms.DataGridView]) { $sum = 0; $mn = 0; foreach ($k in $c.Columns) { if ($k.Visible) { $sum += $k.Width; $mn += $k.MinimumWidth } }
        # R14 (R41): which open it was; R16 (R43 T1): and the sum of the column minimums, to tell a fit that did not run from a fill that overflowed
        if ($sum -gt $c.ClientSize.Width + 1) { $ui.LayBad.Add('LAYOUT ' + $wn.Cur + ' grid ' + $c.AccessibleName + ' columns need ' + $sum + ', the grid has ' +
            $c.ClientSize.Width + ' (column minimums ' + $mn + ')' + ' (open: ' + $wn.OpenKind + ')') }
        $edge = & $wn.EdgeCheck $c $wn.Cur   # R11 (R38): no chip or text ends closer than a scroll bar's width to the grid's right edge
        if ($edge) { $ui.LayBad.Add($edge) } }
      elseif ($c.Controls.Count) { $st.Push($c) } } }
  $logicalW = [int]($form.ClientSize.Width / ([math]::Max(0.5, $ui.Dpi / 96.0)))
  if ($logicalW -ge 1280 -and $main.HorizontalScroll.Visible) { $ui.LayBad.Add('LAYOUT ' + $wn.Cur + ' the main column scrolls sideways at ' + $form.ClientSize.Width + 'x' + $form.ClientSize.Height) }
  if ($main.VerticalScroll.Visible) { $wn.Scrolled[$wn.Cur] = 1 } }
$wn.Scrolled = @{}
$wn.Build = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  Builds the check bar, the rail and every card once, with the layout self-check, the grid check and the accessible-name
  check on each card; $Each (when given) runs after each card with its key (the -Measure run).
  .DESCRIPTION
  R31 W4: while each card is on the page, a picture of the window is saved ($wn.SavePng, measure part) when
  $wn.PngDir is set. This runs before the person sees the window (it is still clear), so nobody loses their place:
  the last card shown is Your Work, where the window starts.
  .PARAMETER Each
  A script block that gets the card key, or nothing.
  #>
  param([scriptblock]$Each)
  & $wn.BuildBar
  & $wn.BuildRail
  & $wn.State 'shown'
  $wn.LastW = $form.ClientSize.Width; $wn.LastH = $form.ClientSize.Height
  foreach ($k in $Cards.Keys) {

    & $wn.SavePng $k
    if ($Each) { & $Each $k } }
  & $wn.NameScan 'rail' $rail; & $wn.NameScan 'bar' $wn.Bar
  $wn.Notice = ''; $wn.Err = ''; & $wn.Show 'home' }
$wn.Recolor = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  Paints the window in the colors for the Windows high-contrast setting (R31 W2): the system colors when it is on,
  the window's own palette when it is off.
  .DESCRIPTION
  At the start it only sets the colors (nothing is built yet). On a change while the window is open it rebuilds the
  rail, the check bar (the current check stays) and the card on the page, so every part takes the new colors; nothing
  happens when the setting did not change. Each change adds one CONTRAST line to the result.
  .PARAMETER When
  'start' or 'changed' (R8: or a name the measure part gives). R10 (R37): a change of the Windows app mode (light or
  dark) adds one THEME line; R11 (R38): it no longer rebuilds, the logo is the Fulcrum one in both modes.
  .PARAMETER Force
  R8 (R35 W7): $true or $false to use instead of the Windows setting (the measure part rebuilds the window both ways
  with no change of the Windows theme); $null: the Windows setting.
  #>
  param([string]$When, $Force = $null)
  $high = $(if ($null -ne $Force) { [bool]$Force } else { [bool][Windows.Forms.SystemInformation]::HighContrast })
  $light = [bool](& $wn.AppsLight)   # R10 (R37): the logo follows the Windows app mode too
  $highNew = ($When -eq 'start' -or $high -ne [bool]$ui.High); $lightNew = ($When -eq 'start' -or $light -ne [bool]$wn.Light)
  if (-not $highNew -and -not $lightNew) { return }
  $wn.Light = $light
  & $ui.UseColors $high; $wn.Fills = & $wn.FillsOf
  $form.BackColor = $pc.surface; $main.BackColor = $pc.surface; $page.BackColor = $pc.surface; $rail.BackColor = $pc.navy
  if ($highNew) { $lines.Add('CONTRAST ' + $When + ': high contrast ' + $(if ($high) { 'on, the window uses the system colors' } else { 'off, the window uses its own colors' })) }
  if ($lightNew) { $lines.Add('THEME ' + $When + ': Windows apps use ' + $(if ($light) { 'light mode, the logo has the Fulcrum colors' } else { 'dark mode, the logo has the Fulcrum colors too' }) +
      $(if ($high) { ' (shown in the system colors while high contrast is on)' } else { '' })) }
  if ($When -eq 'start' -or -not $highNew) { return }   # R11: an app mode change alone changes no color of the window
  $form.SuspendLayout()
  foreach ($x in @($rail.Controls)) { $rail.Controls.Remove($x); $x.Dispose() }
  $wn.RailBtn = @(); & $wn.BuildRail
  $form.Controls.Remove($wn.Bar); $wn.Bar.Dispose(); & $wn.BuildBar
  $form.ResumeLayout($true)
  & $wn.KeepClear   # R13: every kept card has the old colors; each builds again at its next open
  & $wn.Show $wn.Cur; $form.Invalidate($true) }
# R7 (R32 W2; R21: MouseWheel handlers, no message filter): a wheel turn anywhere on the main column scrolls the grid under
# the pointer while that grid can still scroll, else the main column; keys and focus are not touched (Add-PfmWheel).
# Puts the handlers on the window and its controls, also on those added later; a failure is a NOTE line, not a stop.
$wn.WheelOn = {
  try { Add-PfmWheel $form $main; $lines.Add('WHEEL on: the mouse wheel scrolls what is under the pointer') }
  catch { $lines.Add('NOTE the mouse-wheel handlers did not start: ' + ([string]$_.Exception.Message)) } }
$wn.Start = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  Starts the window when it is first shown: its place, its scale, its smallest size, its colors, every card once (with
  the card pictures), then Your Work.
  .DESCRIPTION
  R31 W2: a change of the Windows high-contrast setting while the window is open runs $wn.Recolor; the handler is added
  here, on the window's own thread (so the event comes back on it), and removed when the window closes ($wn.Hook).
  R7 (R32 W2): the mouse-wheel handlers start here ($wn.WheelOn); they go with the window when it closes.
  #>
  & $wn.LoadBounds
  & $ui.FormDpi; $ui.Scaled = $true   # R11 (UI standard v1): the form has its scale now, as RADE's window sets it; button sizes follow it
  $form.MinimumSize = [Drawing.Size]::new((& $wn.Sc 800), (& $wn.Sc 560))
  & $wn.Recolor 'start'
  $wn.PngDir = $dir
  & $wn.Build $null
  & $wn.PngLines
  $wn.Pref = [Microsoft.Win32.UserPreferenceChangedEventHandler]{
    try { & $wn.Recolor 'changed' } catch { $lines.Add('NOTE the colors were not re-applied: ' + ([string]$_.Exception.Message)) } }
  try { [Microsoft.Win32.SystemEvents]::add_UserPreferenceChanged($wn.Pref) } catch { $lines.Add('NOTE no high-contrast change event: ' + ([string]$_.Exception.Message)); $wn.Pref = $null }
  & $wn.WheelOn
  & $wn.OpenLast   # R12: the card of the last close (before Ready, so its open is not counted as the person's)
  $wn.Ready = $true; $form.Opacity = 1
  try { $form.TopMost = $true; $form.Activate(); $form.TopMost = $false } catch { $null = $_ } }
$wn.Hook = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  Adds the window's events: start when shown, re-layout on a new size, Esc and Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+5, save the place on close,
  and remove the high-contrast handler of $wn.Start when the window has closed.
  .DESCRIPTION
  Esc opens the card's Up card (back: the card before a modal one); Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+5 open the rail items in order.
  A window that cannot be built adds a STOPPED line, sets exit code 1 and closes.
  #>
  $form.Add_Shown({ try { & $wn.Start } catch {
        $lines.Add('STOPPED: the window could not be built (' + (ConvertTo-Masked ([string]$_.Exception.Message) $who.Secret) + ')'); $script:code = 1; try { $form.Close() } catch { $null = $_ } } })
  $form.Add_SizeChanged({ if ($wn.Ready) { & $wn.BarLayout; $wn.SizeTimer.Stop(); $wn.SizeTimer.Start() } })
  $form.Add_KeyDown({
      if ($_.KeyCode -eq 'Escape') {
        $up = [string]$Cards[$wn.Cur].Up; if ($up -eq 'back') { $up = $wn.Prev }
        if ($up -and $wn.Cur -ne 'home') { $wn.Notice = ''; $wn.Err = ''; & $wn.Show $up }
        $_.Handled = $true; $_.SuppressKeyPress = $true }
      elseif ($_.Control -and $_.KeyCode -ge [Windows.Forms.Keys]::D1 -and $_.KeyCode -le [Windows.Forms.Keys]::D5) {
        $n = [int]$_.KeyCode - [int][Windows.Forms.Keys]::D1; $wn.Notice = ''; $wn.Err = ''; & $wn.Show ([string]$RailItems[$n].Go); $_.Handled = $true; $_.SuppressKeyPress = $true } })
  $form.Add_FormClosing({ & $wn.State 'close'; & $wn.SaveBounds; & $wn.SaveLast; & $wn.TimeLines; & $wn.FeedbackList })
  $form.Add_FormClosed({ if ($wn.Pref) { try { [Microsoft.Win32.SystemEvents]::remove_UserPreferenceChanged($wn.Pref) } catch { $null = $_ }; $wn.Pref = $null } }) }
'@ }

<#
.SYNOPSIS
  90-161.Z Task 22 r21, part "bar": the check bar of the PFM window, with the in-window checks and the click-through of
  every screen (round R41; PFM 20 Nov 26, docs/reviews/2026-11-21-r41-plan.md row 3).
.DESCRIPTION
  The check bar (PFM 17 Nov 26) sits at the bottom of the window and is always visible: the checks show one at a time,
  with Pass and Fail; no list to remember. Pass or Fail moves to the next step; the answers go to the result file.
  R14 moved it here from the window part (600-line cap) and adds the click-through: after the 4 checks of the cards
  part ($Checks), one step per card ($Walk, Get-WalkPlan in the cards part), in order. Each step names the one rail
  item, button or crumb link that opens the next card from the card before it; a card that no such selection opens
  gets the link "Open this screen" on the bar, shown only on its step. The window notes each card the person opens
  while its step is shown ($wn.WalkSeen, called by $wn.Show in the window part). A step passes when the person
  selected Pass while the card had been opened on that step; Pass on a card that was not opened is a FAIL (not
  opened). Feedback (the feedback part) stays on the bar on every screen. -Again has no click-through ($Walk is empty).
  R15 (R42 T1; R41 finding 4: screens 10 and 11 did not open): "Open this screen" also shows while the screen shown is not
  the one a button step starts on ($wn.OpenShow), and an open by the person that stops adds a NOTE line ($wn.OpenFail).
  R17 (round R44 T4; R43 findings 4 and 6): the step text never reaches the links "Open this screen" and "Feedback": the text
  has the room that is left (no least width that can push it onto a link), the links are in front of it, and a text box that
  is wider than its room is cut back after each step ($wn.BarLayout, $wn.BarFit); the card that shows when the click-through
  starts counts as opened for walk step 1 ($wn.BarShow).
  Inputs: $form, $main, $ui, $wn, $pc, $Cards, $Checks, $Walk, $lines. Outputs: the $wn members below and, at the end
  of a run, the WALK lines ($wn.WalkLines; the main script adds them to the result).
  Run: not alone; 90161Z-T22-pfm-window-r21.ps1 dot-sources it from its own folder inside its try block.
  Network: none.
  Writes: none.
  Credentials: none.
