# The steps of the bar: the checks, then the click-through. $wn.CheckAt is the step shown; the answers are kept by step.
$wn.CheckAt = 0; $wn.Answers = New-Object 'string[]' $Checks.Count
$wn.WalkAns = New-Object 'string[]' $Walk.Count; $wn.WalkOpen = New-Object 'bool[]' $Walk.Count
# The number of steps on the bar.
$wn.StepCount = { return ($Checks.Count + $Walk.Count) }
# The click-through step shown ($Walk index), or -1 while a check (or the closing line) is shown.
$wn.WalkAt = { $j = [int]$wn.CheckAt - $Checks.Count; if ($j -ge 0 -and $j -lt $Walk.Count) { return $j }; return -1 }
# R14: notes that card $Key opened while its click-through step is shown (the person opened it; $wn.Show calls this).
$wn.WalkSeen = { param([string]$Key) $j = & $wn.WalkAt; if ($j -ge 0 -and [string]$Walk[$j].Key -eq $Key) { $wn.WalkOpen[$j] = $true }; & $wn.OpenShow; & $wn.FrameSet }
# R18 (the PFM, 26 Nov 26, R45 comment 6b): a step that names one part of the screen has Target (the accessible name of its control; the
# cards part, Get-WalkPlan). While that step and its card show, the control has a 2 px frame in the primary blue (docs/palette.json).
# The frame is drawn by the control's own Paint event, on its edge, so it follows the layout, the scroll and a resize and needs no extra
# control; it works for a control that paints itself through Paint (a grid, a panel), not for a text box. $wn.FrameName is the name
# framed now ('' for none); $wn.FrameCtl the control; $wn.FrameHooked the controls that already have the Paint handler.
$wn.FrameName = ''; $wn.FrameCtl = $null; $wn.FrameHooked = New-Object System.Collections.ArrayList
# Draws the frame on the control $s when it is the one named by $wn.FrameName. Paint event handler.
$wn.FramePaint = { param($s, $e)
  if (-not $wn.FrameName -or [string]$s.AccessibleName -cne [string]$wn.FrameName) { return }
  try { $pn = New-Object System.Drawing.Pen($pc.primary, [single](& $wn.Sc 2)); $pn.Alignment = [Drawing.Drawing2D.PenAlignment]::Inset
    $e.Graphics.DrawRectangle($pn, 0, 0, ($s.ClientSize.Width - 1), ($s.ClientSize.Height - 1)); $pn.Dispose() } catch { $null = $_ } }   # a paint never stops the window
# Finds the control with accessible name $Name on the page shown. Takes the name; gives back the control or $null.
$wn.FrameFind = { param([string]$Name)
  $st = New-Object System.Collections.Stack; $st.Push($page)
  while ($st.Count) { foreach ($c in $st.Pop().Controls) { if ([string]$c.AccessibleName -ceq $Name) { return $c }; if ($c.Controls.Count) { $st.Push($c) } } }
  return $null }
# Sets the frame for the step and the card shown: on the target of the click-through step when its card shows, else off. Called
# when a step shows ($wn.BarShow) and when a card shows ($wn.WalkSeen). The frame leaves when the walk moves on.
$wn.FrameSet = {
  $j = & $wn.WalkAt; $name = ''
  if ($j -ge 0 -and $Walk[$j].Target -and [string]$Walk[$j].Key -eq [string]$wn.Cur) { $name = [string]$Walk[$j].Target }
  $wn.FrameName = $name; $new = $(if ($name) { & $wn.FrameFind $name } else { $null })
  if ($new -and -not $wn.FrameHooked.Contains($new)) { $new.Add_Paint($wn.FramePaint); [void]$wn.FrameHooked.Add($new) }
  foreach ($c in @($wn.FrameCtl, $new)) { if ($c) { $c.Invalidate() } }
  $wn.FrameCtl = $new }
# R15 (R41 finding 4: one screen that did not open left the next step on a screen without its button): the link "Open
# this screen" shows on a step that needs it, and on any step while the screen shown is not the one the step starts on.
$wn.OpenShow = { if (-not $wn.OpenLink) { return }; $j = & $wn.WalkAt
  $wn.OpenLink.Visible = ($j -ge 0 -and ([string]$Walk[$j].Via -eq 'open' -or ([string]$Walk[$j].Via -ne 'rail' -and $Walk[$j].From -and [string]$Walk[$j].From -ne [string]$wn.Cur))) }
$wn.BarShow = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  Shows the step of the bar: a check (its number and text) or a click-through screen, with Pass and Fail, or the closing
  line when all are answered. The link "Open this screen" shows only on a click-through step that needs it.
  #>
  $i = [int]$wn.CheckAt; $j = & $wn.WalkAt
  if ($i -lt $Checks.Count) {
    $wn.BarNo.Text = 'Check ' + ($i + 1) + ' of ' + $Checks.Count; $wn.BarText.Text = [string]$Checks[$i].Text
    $wn.BarPass.Visible = $true; $wn.BarFail.Visible = $true }
  elseif ($j -ge 0) {
    $wn.BarNo.Text = 'Screen ' + ($j + 1) + ' of ' + $Walk.Count; $wn.BarText.Text = [string]$Walk[$j].Text
    $wn.BarPass.Visible = $true; $wn.BarFail.Visible = $true
    # R17 (R43 finding 6: the window opens on the card of step 1, so the person cannot open it on that step and the walk counted
    # a Pass as "not opened"): the card that shows when step 1 shows counts as opened.
    if ($j -eq 0 -and [string]$wn.Cur -eq [string]$Walk[0].Key) { $wn.WalkOpen[0] = $true } }
  else {
    $wn.BarNo.Text = 'Checks'; $wn.BarText.Text = $script:ChecksDone   # R13: names no card (the -Again check names the card closed on)
    $wn.BarPass.Visible = $false; $wn.BarFail.Visible = $false }
  & $wn.BarFit; & $wn.OpenShow; & $wn.FrameSet }
# R17 (R43 finding 4): the room of the step text, set by $wn.BarLayout (0 until the first layout).
$wn.BarTw = 0
# R17: cuts the step text box back to its room. A text box takes its size from its text when the text changes (the UI part,
# a few pixels past the wrap width), so this runs after each step and after the layout.
$wn.BarFit = { if ($wn.BarTw -gt 0 -and $wn.BarText -and $wn.BarText.Width -gt $wn.BarTw) { $wn.BarText.Size = [Drawing.Size]::new($wn.BarTw, $wn.BarText.Height) } }
# Keeps the answer (PASS or FAIL) to the step shown and shows the next one.
$wn.Answer = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  Keeps the answer $Result (PASS or FAIL) for the step shown, then shows the next step.
  .DESCRIPTION
  R16: a look step counts as opened when its card shows. A click-through step answered while its card never opened
  adds a NOTE line, so the result says why the step has no open.
  .PARAMETER Result
  PASS or FAIL, from the bar buttons.
  #>
  param([string]$Result)
  if ($wn.CheckAt -ge (& $wn.StepCount)) { return }
  $j = & $wn.WalkAt
  # R16: a look step asks about the card the person is on: it counts as opened when that card shows
  if ($j -ge 0 -and [string]$Walk[$j].Via -eq 'look' -and [string]$wn.Cur -eq [string]$Walk[$j].Key) { $wn.WalkOpen[$j] = $true }
  # R16 (R42 finding 3: step12 was answered with no click, so no open failed and no line was written): an answer on a step whose card never opened leaves a NOTE
  if ($j -ge 0 -and -not $wn.WalkOpen[$j]) {
    $lines.Add('NOTE screen ' + ($j + 1) + ' of ' + $Walk.Count + ' (' + [string]$Walk[$j].Key + ') was answered ' + $Result +
      ' without an open: the window shows ' + [string]$wn.Cur) }
  if ($j -ge 0) { $wn.WalkAns[$j] = $Result } else { $wn.Answers[$wn.CheckAt] = $Result }
  $wn.CheckAt++
  & $wn.BarShow }
# R14: the link "Open this screen" opens the card of the click-through step shown, as a person's open.
$wn.OpenStep = {
  $j = & $wn.WalkAt; if ($j -lt 0) { return }
  if (-not (& $ui.Settled)) { & $wn.IgnoreNote 'the link Open this screen'; return }
  $script:presses++; $wn.Notice = ''; $wn.Err = ''; $k = [string]$Walk[$j].Key
  try { & $wn.Show $k } catch { & $wn.OpenFail $k $_ }
  & $wn.OpenCheck $k }
# R15 (R41 finding 4: 2 screens did not open, and the result did not say why): a NOTE line when an open by the person stops.
$wn.OpenFail = { param([string]$Key, $Err) $m = [string]$Err.Exception.Message
  $lines.Add('NOTE the screen ' + $Key + ' did not open: ' + $m.Substring(0, [Math]::Min(160, $m.Length))) }
# R16 (R42 finding 3: step12 did not open and the result had no CARDTIME line and no NOTE line): every way an open can fail
# leaves a NOTE. The guard that holds a click in the first $ui.GuardMs ms after a card changed returned with no line; it
# writes one now ($wn.IgnoreNote, at most 12 lines), and an open that returns with no error while the window stays on the old
# card writes one ($wn.OpenCheck). $Where names the control that was clicked; $Key the card that should show.
$wn.IgnoreN = 0
# Writes a NOTE for a click that the guard held ($Where: the control), at most 12 times in a run.
$wn.IgnoreNote = { param([string]$Where)
  if ($wn.IgnoreN -ge 12) { return }; $wn.IgnoreN++
  $ms = [int]($ui.Clock.Elapsed.TotalMilliseconds - [double]$ui.CardAt)
  $lines.Add('NOTE a click on ' + $Where + ' was not used: the card ' + [string]$wn.Cur + ' changed ' + $ms + ' ms before (the guard holds a click for ' + [int]$ui.GuardMs + ' ms)') }
# Writes a NOTE when the window does not show card $Key after an open that returned with no error.
$wn.OpenCheck = { param([string]$Key)
  if ($Key -and [string]$wn.Cur -ne $Key) { $lines.Add('NOTE the screen ' + $Key + ' did not open: the window stayed on ' + [string]$wn.Cur) } }
$wn.BarLayout = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  Lays out the check bar for the window width: the step text at the left, as tall as the longest step needs, and Pass
  and Fail at the right, centered in the bar.
  .DESCRIPTION
  R10 (R37, B13): the Feedback link sits left of Pass, in the same place on every card. R14: the link "Open this
  screen" sits left of Feedback; its room is kept on every step, so the text and Feedback never move. The height comes
  from the longest check or click-through text, so the bar keeps one height through the whole run.
  #>
  if (-not $wn.Bar) { return }
  $w = $form.ClientSize.Width; $pad = & $wn.Sc 16; $gap = & $wn.Sc 8
  $pw = [int]$wn.BarPass.Width; $fw = [int]$wn.BarFail.Width   # R11 (B1): the fixed RADE sizes
  $bh = [math]::Max($wn.BarPass.Height, $wn.BarFail.Height)
  $kw = $(if ($wn.FbLink) { [math]::Max($wn.FbLink.GetPreferredSize(([Drawing.Size]::new(0, 0))).Width, $wn.FbLink.MinimumSize.Width) + 2 * $gap } else { 0 })
  $ow = $(if ($wn.OpenLink) { [math]::Max($wn.OpenLink.GetPreferredSize(([Drawing.Size]::new(0, 0))).Width, $wn.OpenLink.MinimumSize.Width) + $gap } else { 0 })
  # R17 (R43 finding 4: the text covered the link "Open this screen"): the text has the room that is left and no more. R16 gave it
  # at least 200 px, which pushed it onto the links when the window was small or the links were wide; the bar gets taller instead.
  $tw = [math]::Max(1, $w - 2 * $pad - $pw - $fw - 2 * $gap - $kw - $ow); $wn.BarTw = $tw
  # R18 (the PFM, 26 Nov 26, R45 comment 6a: the sentence ended "...opens and" when "Open this screen" showed): a text box is as wide as its
  # wrap width plus the 4 px its edit control keeps ($ui.TextSize), and $wn.BarFit cut it back to $tw, so the edit control wrapped 4 px
  # earlier than the height was measured and the last line fell out of the box. The wrap width is now $tw less those 4 px, for the
  # height and for the box, so the box is $tw wide, as the height was measured, and a long sentence takes one more line (the bar grows).
  $ww = [math]::Max(1, $tw - 2 * (& $wn.Sc 4))   # 2 x 4 px: wrapped, the box is the wrap width + 4; on one line, its text + 8; never past $tw
  $th = 0; foreach ($c in @(@($Checks) + @($Walk))) { $m = & $ui.Meas ([string]$c.Text) $ui.F.Body $ww; $th = [math]::Max($th, [int]$m.Height) }
  $th += (& $wn.Sc 6)
  $nh = [int]$wn.BarNo.PreferredSize.Height
  $wn.Bar.Height = [math]::Max($bh + 2 * $pad, $pad + $nh + (& $wn.Sc 2) + $th + $pad)
  $wn.BarNo.Location = [Drawing.Point]::new($pad, $pad)
  $wn.BarText.Location = [Drawing.Point]::new($pad, ($pad + $nh + (& $wn.Sc 2))); & $ui.SetWrap $wn.BarText $ww; $wn.BarText.Size = [Drawing.Size]::new($tw, $th)
  $by = [int](($wn.Bar.Height - $bh) / 2)
  $wn.BarPass.Location = [Drawing.Point]::new(($w - $pad - $fw - $gap - $pw), $by); $wn.BarFail.Location = [Drawing.Point]::new(($w - $pad - $fw), $by)
  if ($wn.FbLink) { $wn.FbLink.Location = [Drawing.Point]::new(($wn.BarPass.Left - $kw + $gap), [int](($wn.Bar.Height - $wn.FbLink.Height) / 2)) }
  if ($wn.OpenLink) { $wn.OpenLink.Location = [Drawing.Point]::new(($wn.BarPass.Left - $kw - $ow + $gap), [int](($wn.Bar.Height - $wn.OpenLink.Height) / 2)) } }
$wn.BuildBar = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  Builds the check bar at the bottom of the window: a line on top, the step number, the step text, Pass and Fail, the
  Feedback link and (R14, when the run has a click-through) the link "Open this screen".
  #>
  $bar = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.Panel; $bar.Dock = 'Bottom'; $bar.BackColor = $ui.C.White; $bar.AccessibleName = 'Check bar'
  $bar.Add_Paint({ try { $pn = New-Object System.Drawing.Pen($pc.line, 1); $_.Graphics.DrawLine($pn, 0, 0, $this.ClientSize.Width, 0); $pn.Dispose() } catch { $null = $_ } })
  $no = & $ui.Label $ui.F.SmallB $ui.C.Gray 0; $no.Visible = $true; $no.AccessibleName = 'Check number'; [void]$bar.Controls.Add($no)
  $tx = & $ui.Text $ui.F.Body $ui.C.Ink 0 'Check'; & $wn.NoCaret $tx; $tx.Visible = $true; [void]$bar.Controls.Add($tx)
  foreach ($n in 'Pass', 'Fail') {
    $x = & $ui.Btn 'action'; $x.Text = $n; & $ui.Style $x ''; $x.AccessibleName = $n; $x.Tag = $n
    $x.Add_SizeChanged({ & $wn.Round $this 4 })
    $x.Add_Click({ $r = ([string]$this.Tag).ToUpperInvariant(); & $wn.Answer $r })
    [void]$bar.Controls.Add($x); if ($n -eq 'Pass') { $wn.BarPass = $x } else { $wn.BarFail = $x } }
  # R10 (R37, B13): Feedback, a link on the bar (the same place on every card); it asks for a comment on the card shown.
  $fb = & $ui.LinkBtn (& $wn.FeedbackText); $fb.AccessibleName = 'Feedback on this card'; $fb.Visible = $true
  $fb.Add_Click({ if (& $ui.Settled) { & $wn.FeedbackAsk $wn.Cur } }); [void]$bar.Controls.Add($fb); $wn.FbLink = $fb
  $wn.OpenLink = $null
  if ($Walk.Count) {   # R14: the click-through's own opener, for a card that no rail item, button or link opens
    $op = & $ui.LinkBtn 'Open this screen'; $op.AccessibleName = 'Open this screen'; $op.Visible = $false
    $op.Add_Click({ & $wn.OpenStep }); [void]$bar.Controls.Add($op); $wn.OpenLink = $op }
  $wn.Bar = $bar; $wn.BarNo = $no; $wn.BarText = $tx
  # R17 (R43 finding 4): the links are in front of the step text, so a text that is too wide can never cover them.
  $fb.BringToFront(); if ($wn.OpenLink) { $wn.OpenLink.BringToFront() }
  $form.Controls.Add($bar); $main.BringToFront()
  & $wn.BarShow; & $wn.BarLayout }
$wn.WalkLines = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  R14: the result lines of the click-through, one WALK line per screen and one summary line.
  .DESCRIPTION
  WALK <n> of <N> <card> PASS (opened by you); FAIL (opened by you), FAIL (not opened) when Pass came on a card that was
  not opened on its step, FAIL (not answered). Then: WALK screens opened by you=<n> of <N>, passed=, failed=, not
  answered=. No lines when the run has no click-through (-Again).
  .OUTPUTS
  The lines (strings).
  #>
  if (-not $Walk.Count) { return @() }
  $out = @(); $op = 0; $ps = 0; $fl = 0; $na = 0
  for ($j = 0; $j -lt $Walk.Count; $j++) {
    $a = [string]$wn.WalkAns[$j]; $seen = [bool]$wn.WalkOpen[$j]; if ($seen) { $op++ }
    $res = $(if ($a -eq 'PASS' -and $seen) { $ps++; 'PASS (opened by you)' } elseif ($a -eq 'PASS') { $fl++; 'FAIL (not opened)' }
      elseif ($a -eq 'FAIL') { $fl++; 'FAIL (' + $(if ($seen) { 'opened by you' } else { 'not opened' }) + ')' } else { $na++; 'FAIL (not answered)' })
    $out += ('WALK ' + ($j + 1) + ' of ' + $Walk.Count + ' ' + $Walk[$j].Key + ' ' + $res) }
  $out += ('WALK screens opened by you=' + $op + ' of ' + $Walk.Count + ' passed=' + $ps + ' failed=' + $fl + ' not answered=' + $na)
  return $out }
'@ }
# ---- File 14 of 39: T22\90161Z-T22-keep-r21.ps1 (from scripts/gov/90161Z-T22-keep-r21.ps1, sha256 b77a4bc1a7e3)

<#
.SYNOPSIS
  90-161.Z Task 22 r21, part "keep": each card of the PFM window is built once and kept; a later open shows the kept
  card again instead of building it again (round R40; PFM 20 Nov 26, R39 finding 2).
.DESCRIPTION
  Why: in R39 every open of a card built all its controls again, 123 to 293 ms before any paint (CARDTIME), and later
  opens were no faster than first opens. A person notices a delay over about 100 ms.
  How: each card is built into its own page (a FlowLayoutPanel in the main column, $wn.NewPage). $page always names
  the page shown, so every part that reads the card on the page (layout self-check, grid fit, measure) is unchanged.
  When the window opens another card, the page shown is hidden and the kept page of that card is shown again, with
  the state the window part keeps for the card on the page ($wn.KeepLoad). A hidden page is not laid out, painted,
  checked or scrolled (Windows Forms skips controls that are not visible).
  When a card is built again (the rules, $wn.KeepSig and $wn.Show in the window part): a kept card is used only when
  it was built for the same page size (page column width and main column height), the same wide or narrow rail, the
  same scale and fonts, and the same note and error line. Showing the card that is already shown (a button note, an
  error line, a resize) always builds it again. A card whose fields the person changed (text, check boxes, choices,
  the filter) is not kept when the window leaves it ($wn.KeepLeave), so it opens clean, as a new build does. A color
  change (high contrast) or a scale pass of the measure part drops every kept card ($wn.KeepClear).
  Times (R13, R39 finding 2): for each open by the person, the build time (from the start of $wn.Show until the card
  is laid out) and the paint time (from the start of $wn.Show until the first Paint of the card's page after it); the
  CARDTIME lines at the close give both, and how many opens used a kept card.
  -Measure: $wn.MeasureKeep opens every card again after the first build and records whether the kept card was used
  and how long the open took (tests/ps/Test-T22Layout.ps1 checks it).
  Inputs: $form, $main, $page, $ui, $wn, $Cards, $lines. Outputs: the $wn members below.
  Run: not alone; 90161Z-T22-pfm-window-r21.ps1 dot-sources it from its own folder inside its try block.
  Network: none.
  Writes: none.
  Credentials: none.
#>
$wn.Kept = @{}   # card key -> @{ Page; Sig; Fonts; State; Grids }: the kept page of each card and what it was built for
$wn.KeepUsed = $false   # $true when the last $wn.Show used a kept card (CARDTIME kept=, -Measure)
# The state of the card on the page that the window part sets while it builds a card, kept with the card's page:
# in $wn (main button, grids, reason box, count line, crumb parts, sections, chip rows) and in $ui (the wrap widths of
# the card text boxes, the framed boxes, the title and the line under it that the layout self-check reads).
$wn.KeepWn = @('Primary', 'Gridsel', 'Gridq', 'Reason', 'CountBox', 'CountText', 'CrumbLink', 'CrumbRest', 'Secs', 'ChipRows', 'HeadH')
$wn.KeepUi = @('Wrap', 'Boxes', 'Sent', 'Kick')
$wn.Times = [ordered]@{}   # card key -> the build times in ms of each open by the person (CARDTIME first=, later-max=)
$wn.Paints = @{}           # card key -> the paint times in ms of each open, -1 until its page painted (paint-first=, paint-later-max=)
$wn.KeptN = @{}            # card key -> how many opens by the person used the kept card (kept=)
$wn.PaintWait = $null      # the open that waits for its first paint: @{ Page; Key; I (its place in Paints); T0 }
$wn.NewPage = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  Makes an empty page for one card in the main column (the settings of the first page in the main script).
  .DESCRIPTION
  A top-down flow that sizes itself to the card. Its Paint event ends the paint time of an open ($wn.Painted).
  .OUTPUTS
  The page (System.Windows.Forms.FlowLayoutPanel), added to $main.
  #>
  $p = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.FlowLayoutPanel; $p.FlowDirection = 'TopDown'; $p.WrapContents = $false; $p.AutoSize = $true
  $p.AutoSizeMode = 'GrowAndShrink'; $p.BackColor = $pc.surface
  $p.Add_Paint({ & $wn.Painted $this })
  [void]$main.Controls.Add($p)
  return $p }
# The first Paint of the page of the open that waits ($wn.PaintWait) ends its paint time; other paints do nothing.
$wn.Painted = { param($P)
  $w = $wn.PaintWait; if (-not $w -or -not [object]::ReferenceEquals($w.Page, $P)) { return }
  $wn.PaintWait = $null; $wn.Paints[$w.Key][$w.I] = [int]($ui.Clock.Elapsed.TotalMilliseconds - $w.T0) }
# What a card is built for (see the header): the page column width and main column height, wide or not, the scale,
# the note and the error line. The fonts are compared by reference ($wn.KeepFind). Takes the page column width.
$wn.KeepSig = { param([int]$Cw) return ([string]$Cw + 'x' + $wn.MainH + '|' + $wn.Wide + '|' + $ui.Dpi + '|' + $wn.Notice + '|' + $wn.Err) }
# The kept card of $Key when it was built for $Sig with the fonts in use and its page still exists, else $null.
$wn.KeepFind = { param([string]$Key, [string]$Sig)
  $e = $wn.Kept[$Key]
  if ($e -and $e.Sig -eq $Sig -and [object]::ReferenceEquals($e.Fonts, $ui.F) -and -not $e.Page.IsDisposed) { return $e }
  return $null }
$wn.KeepSave = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  Keeps the card just built on the page: the page, what it was built for, the fonts, its state and its grids.
  .PARAMETER Key
  The card key.
  .PARAMETER Sig
  What it was built for ($wn.KeepSig).
  #>
  param([string]$Key, [string]$Sig)
  $st = @{}; foreach ($n in $wn.KeepWn) { $st['wn.' + $n] = $wn[$n] }; foreach ($n in $wn.KeepUi) { $st['ui.' + $n] = $ui[$n] }
  $gs = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]; $todo = New-Object System.Collections.Stack; $todo.Push($page)
  while ($todo.Count) { foreach ($c in $todo.Pop().Controls) { if ($c -is [Windows.Forms.DataGridView]) { $gs.Add($c) } elseif ($c.Controls.Count) { $todo.Push($c) } } }
  $wn.Kept[$Key] = @{ Page = $page; Sig = $Sig; Fonts = $ui.F; State = $st; Grids = $gs.ToArray() } }
# Puts back the state of kept card $E ($wn.KeepSave) for the card on the page.
$wn.KeepLoad = { param($E)
  foreach ($n in $wn.KeepWn) { $wn[$n] = $E.State['wn.' + $n] }; foreach ($n in $wn.KeepUi) { $ui[$n] = $E.State['ui.' + $n] } }
# A kept card shown again starts as a new build does: no grid row selected, each grid at its first row.
$wn.KeepReset = { param($E)
  foreach ($g in @($E.Grids)) { try { $g.ClearSelection(); if ($g.RowCount -gt 0) { $g.FirstDisplayedScrollingRowIndex = 0 } } catch { $null = $_ } } }
# True when page $P is the page of a kept card.
$wn.IsKept = { param($P) foreach ($e in @($wn.Kept.Values)) { if ([object]::ReferenceEquals($e.Page, $P)) { return $true } }; return $false }
# Forgets the kept card of $Key. Its page goes now when it is hidden; the page shown goes when the next page replaces it
# ($wn.PageSwap), so the controls of the page shown are never disposed under it.
$wn.KeepDrop = { param([string]$Key)
  $e = $wn.Kept[$Key]; if (-not $e) { return }
  $wn.Kept.Remove($Key)
  if (-not [object]::ReferenceEquals($e.Page, $page) -and -not $e.Page.IsDisposed) { [void]$main.Controls.Remove($e.Page); $e.Page.Dispose() } }
# Forgets every kept card (a color change, a scale pass of the measure part): the next open of each card builds it.
$wn.KeepClear = { foreach ($k in @($wn.Kept.Keys)) { & $wn.KeepDrop $k } }
# The window leaves the card on the page: when the person changed one of its fields, it is not kept (it opens clean).
$wn.KeepLeave = { if ($wn.Cur -and @($wn.Field.Keys).Count) { & $wn.KeepDrop $wn.Cur } }
$wn.PageSwap = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  Shows page $New in place of the page shown: the page shown is hidden when it is kept, else removed and disposed.
  .DESCRIPTION
  $page names the page shown from here on (every part reads the card on the page through it).
  .PARAMETER New
  The page to show (a new page, or the page of a kept card).
  #>
  param($New)
  $old = $page
  if ([object]::ReferenceEquals($old, $New)) { return }
  if ($old -and -not $old.IsDisposed) {
    $old.Visible = $false
    if (-not (& $wn.IsKept $old)) { [void]$main.Controls.Remove($old); $old.Dispose() } }
  $script:page = $New; $New.Visible = $true }
$wn.KeepTime = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  Notes one open by the person: its build time now, and its paint time when its page first paints ($wn.Painted).
  .PARAMETER Key
  The card key.
  .PARAMETER T0
  When $wn.Show started ($ui.Clock, ms).
  #>
  param([string]$Key, [double]$T0)
  if (-not $wn.Times.Contains($Key)) { $wn.Times[$Key] = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[int]; $wn.Paints[$Key] = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[int]; $wn.KeptN[$Key] = 0 }
  $wn.Times[$Key].Add([int]($ui.Clock.Elapsed.TotalMilliseconds - $T0)); $wn.Paints[$Key].Add(-1)
  if ($wn.KeepUsed) { $wn.KeptN[$Key]++ }
  $wn.PaintWait = @{ Page = $page; Key = $Key; I = $wn.Paints[$Key].Count - 1; T0 = $T0 }; $page.Invalidate() }
$wn.TimeLines = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  R12 (R38 finding 3), R13 (R39 finding 2): one CARDTIME line for each card the person opened.
  .DESCRIPTION
  first= and later-max=: the build time of the first open and the slowest later open, in ms (as r12). paint-first= and
  paint-later-max=: the same for the paint time (none: the page did not paint before the next open or the close).
  opens=: the opens; kept=: the opens that showed the kept card.
  #>
  foreach ($k in @($wn.Times.Keys)) { $v = @($wn.Times[$k]); $p = @($wn.Paints[$k])
    $later = $(if ($v.Count -gt 1) { ' later-max=' + (@($v | Select-Object -Skip 1 | Measure-Object -Maximum).Maximum) } else { '' })
    $pl = @($p | Select-Object -Skip 1 | Where-Object { $_ -ge 0 })
    $pf = ' paint-first=' + $(if ($p[0] -ge 0) { $p[0] } else { 'none' })
    $plm = $(if ($v.Count -gt 1) { ' paint-later-max=' + $(if ($pl.Count) { (@($pl | Measure-Object -Maximum).Maximum) } else { 'none' }) } else { '' })
    $lines.Add('CARDTIME ' + $k + ' first=' + $v[0] + $later + $pf + $plm + ' opens=' + $v.Count + ' kept=' + $wn.KeptN[$k] +
      ' (ms from the open: build until laid out, paint until its first paint; a resize counts as an open)') }
  if (-not $wn.Times.Count) { $lines.Add('CARDTIME none (no card opened after the start)') } }
$wn.MeasureKeep = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  The -Measure run: opens every card once more after the first build and records whether its kept card was used.
  .DESCRIPTION
  Runs after $wn.Build (every card built and kept at this size). The card on the page goes last: showing the card that
  is shown builds it again (the window part's rule), so it is opened after another card, as a person opens it. Then
  Your Work is shown again.
  .OUTPUTS
  One table per card: Key, Kept (the kept card was shown), Ms (the open, from the start of $wn.Show until it returned).
  #>
  $out = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]
  foreach ($k in @(@($Cards.Keys | Where-Object { $_ -ne $wn.Cur }) + @($wn.Cur))) {
    $wn.Notice = ''; $wn.Err = ''; $t0 = $ui.Clock.Elapsed.TotalMilliseconds; & $wn.Show $k
    $r = [ordered]@{}; $r['Key'] = [string]$k; $r['Kept'] = [bool]$wn.KeepUsed; $r['Ms'] = [int]($ui.Clock.Elapsed.TotalMilliseconds - $t0); $out.Add($r)
    [Windows.Forms.Application]::DoEvents() }
  $wn.Notice = ''; $wn.Err = ''; & $wn.Show 'home'
  return $out.ToArray() }

<#
.SYNOPSIS
  90-161.Z Task 22 r21, part "feedback": Feedback on every card of the PFM window (UI standard B13, PFM 19 Nov 26).
.DESCRIPTION
  R14 (R41; PFM 20 Nov 26): Feedback stays on every screen of the click-through; the picture of a comment is not saved
  when the card shows a site row without a fake-data marker (Get-SiteUnmarked in the site part).
  R11 (R38; PFM 20 Nov 26): only the revision in the file names changed (90161Z-T22-feedback-<card>-r16.*).
  The window part puts the Feedback link on the check bar (the same place on every card) and calls $wn.FeedbackAsk on
  a click and $wn.FeedbackList at the close; the -Measure run calls $wn.MeasureFeedback (below), which saves one FAKE

  Inputs: $form, $ui, $wn, $who, $dir, $Rev, $lines. Outputs: the $wn members below.
  Run: not alone; 90161Z-T22-pfm-window-r21.ps1 dot-sources it from its own folder inside its try block.
  Network: none.
  Writes: per saved comment 90161Z-T22-feedback-<card>-r21.txt and .png, or the .txt only when a shown row has no fake-data

# R10 (R37; PFM 19 Nov 26, UI standard B13): Feedback on every card. The link opens a small comment box; Save writes the
# comment and a picture of the window as it was when the link was selected, into the T22 folder (the round sends them):
# 90161Z-T22-feedback-<card>-r21.txt and .png (the .txt only when a shown row has no fake-data marker; a second comment on the same card, in this run or an earlier window run of
# the same round: <card>-2, and so on). Each save adds a FEEDBACK line to the result file; at the close each run adds its
# lines to 90161Z-T22-feedback-r21.txt (every comment file, or none), so the round always finds one feedback file and a
# second run keeps the first run's lines. With -Measure the files go to the folder of the measure file.
$wn.FeedbackN = @{}; $wn.FeedbackAll = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]
$wn.FeedbackPng = @{}   # R14: base name -> $true when its picture was saved (the marker check can block it)
# Saves window picture $Shot as a PNG file at $Path (one place, so tests/check_t22_r18.py can stand in for it off Windows).
$wn.PngSave = { param($Shot, [string]$Path) $Shot.Save($Path, [System.Drawing.Imaging.ImageFormat]::Png) }
# The link text: "Feedback", and how many comments were saved.
$wn.FeedbackText = { if ($wn.FeedbackAll.Count) { return ('Feedback (' + $wn.FeedbackAll.Count + ' saved)') }; return 'Feedback' }
# The folder the feedback files go to: the T22 folder, or the measure folder.
$wn.FeedbackDir = { if ($dir) { return $dir }; return [string]$wn.PngDir }
# The base name of comment $N on card $Key: 90161Z-T22-feedback-<card>-r21, or <card>-<N> from the second one on.
# $wn.FeedbackSave raises $N past every name whose .txt or .png is already in the folder (an earlier window run).
$wn.FeedbackName = { param([string]$Key, [int]$N)
  return ('90161Z-T22-feedback-' + $Key + $(if ($N -gt 1) { '-' + $N } else { '' }) + '-' + $Rev) }
# A picture of the whole window as it is now (Control.DrawToBitmap). The caller disposes it.
$wn.Snapshot = {
  $bm = New-Object System.Drawing.Bitmap([math]::Max(1, $form.Width), [math]::Max(1, $form.Height))
  $form.DrawToBitmap($bm, (New-Object System.Drawing.Rectangle(0, 0, $bm.Width, $bm.Height))); return $bm }
$wn.FeedbackSave = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  Saves one comment on card $Key: the text file and the window picture $Shot, in the feedback folder.
  .DESCRIPTION
  The comment is masked with the shared rules (Hide-Site: e-mail addresses, the RADE site, URLs, .mil hosts and GUIDs;
  then the DODID shows as <DODID>, like every result line). The name is new: a name whose .txt or .png is already in the
  folder is skipped. Adds a FEEDBACK line to the result and the base name to $wn.FeedbackAll, and shows the new count
  on the Feedback link. A save that fails is a NOTE line, not a stop.
  .PARAMETER Key
  The card key.
  .PARAMETER Text
  The comment as typed.
  .PARAMETER Shot
  The window picture (a Bitmap).
  .OUTPUTS
  The base name of the two files, or '' when nothing was saved.
  #>
  param([string]$Key, [string]$Text, $Shot)
  $into = & $wn.FeedbackDir
  if (-not $into) { $lines.Add('NOTE feedback not saved: no folder'); return '' }
  try {
    $n = 1 + [int]$wn.FeedbackN[$Key]; $base = & $wn.FeedbackName $Key $n
    while ((Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $into ($base + '.txt'))) -or (Test-Path -LiteralPath (Join-Path $into ($base + '.png')))) {
      $n++; $base = & $wn.FeedbackName $Key $n }   # an earlier window run of the round saved this name: never overwrite it
    $wn.FeedbackN[$Key] = $n
    $bad = Get-SiteUnmarked $Key   # R14 (R41): no picture of a card with a site row that has no fake-data marker
    if ($bad -gt 0) { $wn.FeedbackPng[$base] = $false }
    else { & $wn.PngSave $Shot (Join-Path $into ($base + '.png')); $wn.FeedbackPng[$base] = $true }
    $t = Hide-Site (([string]$Text).Trim()) ([string]$env:RADE_SITE); if ($who) { $t = ConvertTo-Masked $t $who.Secret }

    Set-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $into ($base + '.txt')) -Value $body -Encoding UTF8

    if ($wn.FeedbackPng[$base]) { $lines.Add('FEEDBACK ' + $Key + ': ' + $base + '.txt and ' + $base + '.png') }
    else { $lines.Add('FEEDBACK ' + $Key + ': ' + $base + '.txt'); $lines.Add('FEEDBACK ' + $Key + ': picture not saved (' + $bad + ' site rows without a fake-data marker)') }

    if ($wn.FbLink) { $wn.FbLink.Text = & $wn.FeedbackText; if ($wn.BarLayout) { & $wn.BarLayout } }
    return $base
  } catch { $lines.Add('NOTE feedback not saved: ' + ([string]$_.Exception.Message)); return '' } }

$wn.SavePng = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  Saves a picture of the window as it shows card $Key (R31 W4): 90161Z-T22-card-<key>-r21.png in $wn.PngDir.
  .DESCRIPTION
  Control.DrawToBitmap at the window's current size; nothing when $wn.PngDir is empty. A picture that cannot be
  saved is a NOTE line in the result, not a stop. The file name is kept in $wn.Pngs.
  R14 (R41): no picture of a card that shows a site row without a fake-data marker (Get-SiteUnmarked, site part); a
  CARDPNG line says so.
  .PARAMETER Key
  The card key (the card on the page).
  #>
  param([string]$Key)
  if (-not $wn.PngDir) { return }
  $name = '90161Z-T22-card-' + $Key + '-' + $Rev + '.png'
  # R14 (R41; PFM 20 Nov 26): a card that shows a site row with no fake-data marker gets no picture (the site part)
  $bad = Get-SiteUnmarked $Key
  if ($bad -gt 0) { $lines.Add('CARDPNG ' + $Key + ' not saved: ' + $bad + ' site rows without a fake-data marker'); return }
  try {
    $bm = New-Object System.Drawing.Bitmap([math]::Max(1, $form.Width), [math]::Max(1, $form.Height))
    try {
      $form.DrawToBitmap($bm, (New-Object System.Drawing.Rectangle(0, 0, $bm.Width, $bm.Height)))
      $bm.Save((Join-Path $wn.PngDir $name), [System.Drawing.Imaging.ImageFormat]::Png); $wn.Pngs.Add($name)
    } finally { $bm.Dispose() }
  } catch { $lines.Add('NOTE card picture not saved: ' + $name + ' (' + ([string]$_.Exception.Message) + ')') } }

$wn.NameScan = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  Notes each button, link, check box, choice, text box and list under $Root that has no accessible name.
  .PARAMETER Card
  The card key (or rail, bar) the controls belong to; it starts each note.
  .PARAMETER Root
  The control whose children are read (the page, the rail or the check bar).
  #>
  param([string]$Card, $Root)
  if (-not $Root) { return }

  while ($st.Count) {
    foreach ($c in $st.Pop().Controls) {
      $named = ($c -is [Windows.Forms.ButtonBase] -or $c -is [Windows.Forms.TextBoxBase] -or $c -is [Windows.Forms.ComboBox])
      if ($named -and -not ([string]$c.AccessibleName).Trim()) {
        $t = ([string]$c.Text).Trim(); if ($t.Length -gt 24) { $t = $t.Substring(0, 24) + '...' }
        $wn.NoName[$Card + '/' + $c.GetType().Name + ' "' + $t + '"'] = 1 }
      if ($c.Controls.Count) { $st.Push($c) } } } }
# The RESULT NAMES line: PASS, or FAIL with the number of controls without a name and which ones.
$wn.NamesLine = {
  if ($wn.NoName.Count -eq 0) { return 'RESULT NAMES PASS' }
  return ('RESULT NAMES FAIL (' + $wn.NoName.Count + ' controls: ' + (@($wn.NoName.Keys) -join ', ') + ')') }
$wn.InkSpan = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  Where the ink of a control starts and ends, left to right, as drawn.
  .DESCRIPTION
  Draws the control into a bitmap and finds the first and the last pixel column that differs from its background by
  more than 90 (the RADE ink rule, $ui.Ink: the sum of the red, green and blue distances).
  .PARAMETER C
  The control.
  .OUTPUTS
  @{ First; Last } in the control's own pixels; -1 when nothing was drawn.
  #>
  param($C)
  $out = @{ First = -1; Last = -1 }
  try {
    $w = [math]::Max(1, $C.Width); $h = [math]::Max(1, $C.Height); $bm = New-Object System.Drawing.Bitmap($w, $h)
    try {
      $C.DrawToBitmap($bm, (New-Object System.Drawing.Rectangle(0, 0, $w, $h))); $bg = $C.BackColor
      for ($x = 0; $x -lt $w; $x++) {
        for ($y = 0; $y -lt $h; $y++) {
          $p = $bm.GetPixel($x, $y)
          if ([math]::Abs($p.R - $bg.R) + [math]::Abs($p.G - $bg.G) + [math]::Abs($p.B - $bg.B) -gt 90) { if ($out.First -lt 0) { $out.First = $x }; $out.Last = $x; break } } }
    } finally { $bm.Dispose() }
  } catch { $null = $_ }
  return $out }
# A color as #RRGGBB.
$wn.Hex = { param($Color) return ('#{0:X2}{1:X2}{2:X2}' -f $Color.R, $Color.G, $Color.B) }
# The color of a button's face as drawn: the pixel 6 px right of and 4 px under its top left corner (inside its edge, above its text).
$wn.FaceColor = { param($B)
  try {
    $bm = New-Object System.Drawing.Bitmap([math]::Max(1, $B.Width), [math]::Max(1, $B.Height))
    try { $B.DrawToBitmap($bm, (New-Object System.Drawing.Rectangle(0, 0, $bm.Width, $bm.Height))); return (& $wn.Hex $bm.GetPixel((& $wn.Sc 6), (& $wn.Sc 4))) } finally { $bm.Dispose() }
  } catch { return '' } }
# A font as a table: name, size in points, style and height in pixels.
$wn.FontFacts = { param($F) return [ordered]@{ Name = $F.Name; Size = [double]$F.SizeInPoints; Style = [string]$F.Style; Height = [int]$F.Height } }
$wn.MeasureCrumb = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  The crumb of the card on the page: its link and rest, their fonts and bounds, and the gap after the link.
  .DESCRIPTION
  GapInk: the empty pixel columns between the last ink of the link (its underline ends with its text) and the first ink
  of the rest (the arrow), as drawn. GapBounds: the distance between the two controls.
  .OUTPUTS
  A table, or $null when the card has no crumb link.
  #>
  $l = $wn.CrumbLink; $t = $wn.CrumbRest; if (-not $l -or -not $t) { return $null }
  $li = & $wn.InkSpan $l; $ti = & $wn.InkSpan $t
  $gap = $(if ($li.Last -ge 0 -and $ti.First -ge 0) { ($t.Left + $ti.First) - ($l.Left + $li.Last) - 1 } else { $null })
  return [ordered]@{ Link = [string]$l.Text; Rest = [string]$t.Text; LinkFont = (& $wn.FontFacts $l.Font); RestFont = (& $wn.FontFacts $t.Font)
    LinkBounds = [string]$l.Bounds; RestBounds = [string]$t.Bounds; LinkInk = $li.Last; RestInk = $ti.First; GapBounds = ($t.Left - $l.Right); GapInk = $gap } }
$wn.LevelPubs = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  R6 (R31b D4): where each grid with a pub column on the page drew its numbers and titles.
  .DESCRIPTION
  Each such grid is drawn once into a bitmap (so its cells are painted now, also off-screen); $wn.PaintPub keeps what
  it drew in the grid's Tag.Drawn, relative to the cell's text rectangle. Rows that are scrolled out of the grid are
  not drawn and not listed.
  R7 (R32 W1): also the head of the pub column (its text, the width it needs and has) and, per row drawn, the widths
  and heights the number and title needed and had ($wn.PaintPub).
  .OUTPUTS
  One table per grid: Grid (its name), Gap (the gap after the widest number), Rows (rows drawn), Head, HeadW, HeadHave
  and, one value per row drawn, Beside, TitleX, NumRight, NumBottom, TitleTop, NumW, NumHave, TitleW, TitleHave, NeedH
  and HaveH.
  #>
  $out = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]; $st = New-Object System.Collections.Stack; $st.Push($page)
  while ($st.Count) {
    foreach ($c in $st.Pop().Controls) {
      if ($c -is [Windows.Forms.DataGridView]) {
        if (-not ($c.Tag -is [hashtable]) -or -not (@($c.Tag.Kind.Values) -contains 'pub')) { continue }
        $c.Tag.Drawn = @{}; $c.Tag.Head = $null
        try { $bm = New-Object System.Drawing.Bitmap([math]::Max(1, $c.Width), [math]::Max(1, $c.Height))
          try { $c.DrawToBitmap($bm, (New-Object System.Drawing.Rectangle(0, 0, $bm.Width, $bm.Height))) } finally { $bm.Dispose() } } catch { $null = $_ }
        $d = @(foreach ($k in @($c.Tag.Drawn.Keys | Sort-Object)) { $c.Tag.Drawn[$k] })
        $g = [ordered]@{}; $g['Grid'] = [string]$c.AccessibleName; $g['Gap'] = [int]$c.Tag.PubGap; $g['Rows'] = $d.Count
        $h = $c.Tag.Head; $g['Head'] = $(if ($h) { [string]$h.Text } else { '' }); $g['HeadW'] = $(if ($h) { [int]$h.W } else { 0 }); $g['HeadHave'] = $(if ($h) { [int]$h.Have } else { 0 })
        foreach ($n in 'Beside', 'TitleX', 'NumRight', 'NumBottom', 'TitleTop', 'NumW', 'NumHave', 'TitleW', 'TitleHave', 'NeedH', 'HaveH') { $g[$n] = @($d | ForEach-Object { $_[$n] }) }
        $out.Add($g) }
      elseif ($c.Controls.Count) { $st.Push($c) } } }
  return $out.ToArray() }
$wn.LevelHeads = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  R8 (R35 W7, R34 open point 5): the column heads of every grid on the page, as the grid drew them.
  .DESCRIPTION
  Each grid is drawn once into a bitmap (so its head is painted now, also off-screen); $wn.PaintCell keeps each head
  it drew in the grid's Tag.Heads: its text in capitals, the width it needs and the width its cell gave it.
  .OUTPUTS
  One table per head: Grid (its name), Col (the column name), Kind, Head (the text), W (needed) and Have.
  #>
  $out = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]; $st = New-Object System.Collections.Stack; $st.Push($page)
  while ($st.Count) {
    foreach ($c in $st.Pop().Controls) {
      if ($c -is [Windows.Forms.DataGridView]) {
        if (-not ($c.Tag -is [hashtable])) { continue }
        $c.Tag.Heads = [ordered]@{}
        try { $bm = New-Object System.Drawing.Bitmap([math]::Max(1, $c.Width), [math]::Max(1, $c.Height))
          try { $c.DrawToBitmap($bm, (New-Object System.Drawing.Rectangle(0, 0, $bm.Width, $bm.Height))) } finally { $bm.Dispose() } } catch { $null = $_ }
        foreach ($k in @($c.Tag.Heads.Keys)) { $h = $c.Tag.Heads[$k]
          $r = [ordered]@{}; $r['Grid'] = [string]$c.AccessibleName; $r['Col'] = [string]$k; $r['Kind'] = [string]$h.Kind; $r['Head'] = [string]$h.Text
          $r['W'] = [int]$h.W; $r['Have'] = [int]$h.Have; $out.Add($r) } }
      elseif ($c.Controls.Count) { $st.Push($c) } } }
  return $out.ToArray() }
$wn.LevelEdges = {

$wn.LevelFacts = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  R6 (R31b D1 to D4): the alignment facts of the card on the page, in page pixels ($wn.TextMid).
  .DESCRIPTION
  Caps (D1): for each Action Status card, the middle of its caption and of the first line of the main card. Crumb (D2):
  the font size and text middle of the crumb's link and rest, or $null when the card has no crumb link. Chips (D3, R7
  W3): for each chip beside text ($wn.ChipRows: check, list, rows, chips, notice), its kind, the middle of the chip and
  of the first line of its text. Pubs (D4, R7 W1): $wn.LevelPubs. Heads (R8 W7): $wn.LevelHeads.
  .OUTPUTS
  A table: Caps, Crumb, Chips, Pubs, Heads, Edges (R11: $wn.LevelEdges).
  #>
  $mainSec = @($wn.Secs | Where-Object { $_.Col -eq 0 }) | Select-Object -First 1
  $line = $(if ($mainSec) { & $wn.FirstLine $mainSec.Card } else { $null })
  $caps = @(foreach ($s in @($wn.Secs | Where-Object { $_.Stretch -and $_.CapBox -and $line })) {
      $c = [ordered]@{}; $c['Cap'] = [string]$s.CapBox.Text; $c['CapMid'] = (& $wn.TextMid $s.CapBox); $c['Line'] = [string]$line.Text; $c['LineMid'] = (& $wn.TextMid $line); $c })
  $crumb = $null; $l = $wn.CrumbLink; $t = $wn.CrumbRest
  if ($l -and $t) { $crumb = [ordered]@{}; $crumb['LinkSize'] = [double]$l.Font.SizeInPoints; $crumb['RestSize'] = [double]$t.Font.SizeInPoints
    $crumb['LinkMid'] = (& $wn.TextMid $l); $crumb['RestMid'] = (& $wn.TextMid $t) }
  $chips = @(foreach ($r in @($wn.ChipRows)) {
      $c = [ordered]@{}; $c['Chip'] = [string]$r.Chip.Text; $c['Kind'] = [string]$r.Kind; $c['ChipMid'] = (& $wn.TextMid $r.Chip)
      # R48: a list or rows chip is compared with the middle of its row (Ref 'row'); every other chip with its text's first line.
      $c['Ref'] = $(if ($r.Row) { 'row' } else { 'first line' }); $c['Line'] = [string]$r.Text.Text
      $c['LineMid'] = $(if ($r.Row) { (& $wn.PageTop $r.Row) + $r.Row.Height / 2.0 } else { (& $wn.TextMid $r.Text) }); $c })
  $f = [ordered]@{}; $f['Caps'] = $caps; $f['Crumb'] = $crumb; $f['Chips'] = $chips; $f['Pubs'] = @(& $wn.LevelPubs); $f['Heads'] = @(& $wn.LevelHeads); $f['Edges'] = @(& $wn.LevelEdges)
  return $f }
# R7 (W1): the cut cells of one measured pub grid $P ($wn.LevelPubs), one short text per row: "row <n> number 120>96"
# when its number, title or lines needed more pixels than the cell gave; none when every cell holds its text.
$wn.PubCut = { param($P)
  $out = @(); $nw = @($P.NumW); $nh = @($P.NumHave); $tw = @($P.TitleW); $th = @($P.TitleHave); $lh = @($P.NeedH); $ch = @($P.HaveH)
  for ($i = 0; $i -lt [int]$P.Rows; $i++) {
    $bad = @(); if ([int]$nw[$i] -gt [int]$nh[$i]) { $bad += ('number ' + $nw[$i] + '>' + $nh[$i]) }
    if ([int]$tw[$i] -gt [int]$th[$i]) { $bad += ('title ' + $tw[$i] + '>' + $th[$i]) }
    if ([int]$lh[$i] -gt [int]$ch[$i]) { $bad += ('height ' + $lh[$i] + '>' + $ch[$i]) }
    if ($bad.Count) { $out += ('row ' + ($i + 1) + ' ' + ($bad -join ', ')) } }
  return $out }
$wn.LevelBad = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  The LAYOUT lines of the layout self-check for D1 to D4 (R6): each fact of $wn.LevelFacts that is out of line.
  .DESCRIPTION
  D1, D2 and D3: two middles more than $Tol apart (D2 also: two font sizes). D4: the titles of a grid start at more than
  one x, or a title in the column starts before the end of the widest number and the gap, or a title under its number
  starts above the number's bottom. A grid with no row drawn has nothing to compare.
  R7 (R32): W1: the head of a pub column needs more width than it has (it would be shortened with dots), or a pub cell
  is cut (its number or title needs more width, or its lines more height, than the cell gave). W3: the D3 rule for
  every chip beside text; the line names the chip's kind.
  R8 (R35 W7): a column head other than the pub head (W1 has that one) needs more width than it has: one line per grid
  that names each cut head.
  .PARAMETER Card
  The card key (it starts each line).
  .PARAMETER F
  The facts ($wn.LevelFacts).
  .PARAMETER Tol
  The tolerance in pixels: 1 px at 100 %, scaled.
  .OUTPUTS
  The LAYOUT lines (none when all is in line).
  #>
  param([string]$Card, $F, [double]$Tol)
  $out = @()
  foreach ($c in @($F.Caps)) { if ([math]::Abs($c.CapMid - $c.LineMid) -gt $Tol) {
      $out += ('LAYOUT ' + $Card + ' D1 caption "' + $c.Cap + '" middle ' + $c.CapMid + ', the first line of the main card ' + $c.LineMid) } }
  $k = $F.Crumb
  if ($k -and ($k.LinkSize -ne $k.RestSize -or [math]::Abs($k.LinkMid - $k.RestMid) -gt $Tol)) {
    $out += ('LAYOUT ' + $Card + ' D2 crumb: link ' + $k.LinkSize + ' pt middle ' + $k.LinkMid + ', rest ' + $k.RestSize + ' pt middle ' + $k.RestMid) }
  foreach ($c in @($F.Chips)) { if ([math]::Abs($c.ChipMid - $c.LineMid) -gt $Tol) {
      $out += ('LAYOUT ' + $Card + ' W3 chip "' + $c.Chip + '" (' + $c.Kind + ') middle ' + $c.ChipMid + ', its ' + $c.Ref + ' middle ' + $c.LineMid) } }
  foreach ($p in @($F.Pubs)) {
    if ($p.Head -and [int]$p.HeadW -gt [int]$p.HeadHave) {
      $out += ('LAYOUT ' + $Card + ' W1 grid ' + $p.Grid + ': the head "' + $p.Head + '" needs ' + $p.HeadW + ' px, has ' + $p.HeadHave) }
    $cut = @(& $wn.PubCut $p)
    if ($cut.Count) { $out += ('LAYOUT ' + $Card + ' W1 grid ' + $p.Grid + ': ' + $cut.Count + ' publication cells cut (' + ($cut -join '; ') + ')') }
    if ([int]$p.Rows -lt 1) { continue }
    $xs = @($p.TitleX | Sort-Object -Unique); $num = [int](@($p.NumRight) | Measure-Object -Maximum).Maximum
    $under = @(for ($i = 0; $i -lt [int]$p.Rows; $i++) { if (-not $p.Beside[$i] -and $p.TitleTop[$i] -lt $p.NumBottom[$i]) { $i } })
    if ($xs.Count -gt 1) { $out += ('LAYOUT ' + $Card + ' D4 grid ' + $p.Grid + ': the titles start at ' + ($xs -join ', ')) }
    elseif ((@($p.Beside) -contains $true) -and [int]$xs[0] -lt $num + [int]$p.Gap) {
      $out += ('LAYOUT ' + $Card + ' D4 grid ' + $p.Grid + ': the titles start at ' + $xs[0] + ', the widest number ends at ' + $num) }
    elseif ($under.Count) { $out += ('LAYOUT ' + $Card + ' D4 grid ' + $p.Grid + ': ' + $under.Count + ' titles start above the bottom of their number') } }
  $cut = @($F.Heads | Where-Object { $_ -and [string]$_.Kind -ne 'pub' -and [int]$_.W -gt [int]$_.Have })
  foreach ($g in @($cut | ForEach-Object { [string]$_.Grid } | Sort-Object -Unique)) {
    $list = @($cut | Where-Object { [string]$_.Grid -eq $g } | ForEach-Object { '"' + $_.Head + '" needs ' + $_.W + ' px, has ' + $_.Have })
    $out += ('LAYOUT ' + $Card + ' W7 grid ' + $g + ': ' + $list.Count + ' column heads cut (' + ($list -join '; ') + ')') }
  return $out }
# The self-check's extra lines (the rade-ui block calls $ui.Measure for each card it checks): D1 to D4, 1 px at 100 %.
$ui.Measure = { param($Card) return @(& $wn.LevelBad $Card (& $wn.LevelFacts) ([math]::Max(1.0, $ui.Dpi / 96.0))) }
$wn.MeasureCard = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  What -Measure records for the card on the page: the crumb, every button and link, every section card, and the
  alignment facts of D1 to D4 (R6).
  .PARAMETER Key
  The card key.
  .OUTPUTS
  A table: Key, Crumb, Buttons (Text, Link, Back, Face, Edge), Sections (Col, Cap, Stretch, Top, Bottom; page pixels),
  Level ($wn.LevelFacts).
  #>
  param([string]$Key)
  $btns = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]; $st = New-Object System.Collections.Stack; $st.Push($page)
  while ($st.Count) {
    foreach ($c in $st.Pop().Controls) {
      if ($c -is [Windows.Forms.Button]) {
        $b = [ordered]@{}; $b['Text'] = [string]$c.Text; $b['Link'] = ([int]$c.FlatAppearance.BorderSize -eq 0)
        $b['Back'] = (& $wn.Hex $c.BackColor); $b['Face'] = (& $wn.FaceColor $c); $b['Edge'] = (& $wn.Hex $c.FlatAppearance.BorderColor)
        $btns.Add($b) }
      if ($c.Controls.Count) { $st.Push($c) } } }
  $pt = $page.RectangleToScreen($page.ClientRectangle).Top
  $secs = @(foreach ($s in $wn.Secs) { $r = $s.Card.RectangleToScreen($s.Card.ClientRectangle)
      [ordered]@{ Col = $s.Col; Cap = $s.Cap; Stretch = $s.Stretch; Top = ($r.Top - $pt); Bottom = ($r.Bottom - $pt) } })
  # One key per statement: Windows PowerShell 5.1 stops on an [ordered] literal that holds a generic list (R30 CI).
  $card = [ordered]@{}; $card['Key'] = $Key; $card['Crumb'] = (& $wn.MeasureCrumb)
  $card['Buttons'] = $btns.ToArray(); $card['Sections'] = $secs; $card['Level'] = (& $wn.LevelFacts)
  return $card }
$wn.MeasureScaled = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  Builds every card again at $K times this scale and gives back the alignment facts of D1 to D4 of each (R6).
  .DESCRIPTION
  As $wn.MeasureHead does for the rail head: the scale ($ui.Dpi), the font factor and every font of $ui.F (with the
  crumb font and the step fonts made from them) are $K times as large, as Windows makes them at that scale. Each card is
  shown and measured ($wn.LevelFacts); a card that cannot be measured keeps its error. Then the scale and the fonts come
  back, Your Work is shown again and the scaled fonts are disposed.
  .PARAMETER K
  The factor (1.5: the PFM's 150 %).
  .OUTPUTS
  A table: K, Dpi, Sc8 (8 px at 100 %, at this scale), Cards (Key, Level or Error) and (R7 W2) Wheel ($wn.MeasureWheel)
  or WheelError.
  #>
  param([double]$K)
  $keep = @{ Dpi = $ui.Dpi; FontK = $ui.FontK; F = $ui.F; Crumb = $wn.CrumbFont; Step = $wn.StepFonts }
  $made = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]; $cards = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]; $res = [ordered]@{}
  try {
    $nf = @{}; foreach ($n in @($keep.F.Keys)) { $o = $keep.F[$n]; $x = New-Object System.Drawing.Font($o.FontFamily, [single]($o.Size * $K), $o.Style); $nf[$n] = $x; $made.Add($x) }
    $ui.Dpi = $keep.Dpi * $K; $ui.FontK = $keep.FontK * $K; $ui.F = $nf; $wn.StepFonts = $null
    $wn.CrumbFont = New-Object System.Drawing.Font($nf.Small, [Enum]::Parse(('System.Drawing.FontStyle' -as [type]), 'Underline')); $made.Add($wn.CrumbFont)
    $res['K'] = $K; $res['Dpi'] = $ui.Dpi; $res['Sc8'] = (& $wn.Sc 8)
    foreach ($key in $Cards.Keys) {
      $c = [ordered]@{}; $c['Key'] = $key
      try { $wn.Notice = ''; $wn.Err = ''; & $wn.Show $key; [Windows.Forms.Application]::DoEvents(); $c['Level'] = (& $wn.LevelFacts); $c['Btn'] = @(& $wn.BtnLines) }
      catch { $c['Error'] = ([string]$_.Exception.Message + ' at ' + (Get-ErrorPlace $_)) }
      $cards.Add($c) }
    # R7 (W2): the mouse wheel at this scale too; a wheel case that cannot run is kept as its error (the test names it).
    try { $res['Wheel'] = (& $wn.MeasureWheel) } catch { $res['Wheel'] = $null; $res['WheelError'] = ([string]$_.Exception.Message + ' at ' + (Get-ErrorPlace $_)) }
  } finally {
    if ($wn.StepFonts -and -not [object]::ReferenceEquals($wn.StepFonts, $keep.Step)) { foreach ($x in @($wn.StepFonts.A) + @($wn.StepFonts.B)) { $made.Add($x) } }
    $ui.Dpi = $keep.Dpi; $ui.FontK = $keep.FontK; $ui.F = $keep.F; $wn.CrumbFont = $keep.Crumb; $wn.StepFonts = $keep.Step
    & $wn.KeepClear; $wn.Notice = ''; $wn.Err = ''; & $wn.Show 'home'   # R13: no kept card keeps the scaled fonts disposed below
    foreach ($x in $made) { try { $x.Dispose() } catch { $null = $_ } } }
  $res['Cards'] = $cards.ToArray()
  return $res }
# R11 (R38; UI standard v1, B1): the B1 lines ($ui.BtnBad) of every shown RADE button of the page, at the scale in use
# (the self-check runs at the window's own scale only; this one runs at 1.25 x and 1.5 x too). None when all are right.
$wn.BtnLines = {
  $out = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[string]; $st = New-Object System.Collections.Stack; $st.Push($page)
  while ($st.Count) { foreach ($c in $st.Pop().Controls) {
      if ($c -is [Windows.Forms.Button] -and $c.Visible -and $ui.BtnKind.ContainsKey($c)) { foreach ($l in @(& $ui.BtnBad 'scaled' ([string]$c.AccessibleName) $c)) { $out.Add([string]$l) } }
      elseif ($c.Controls.Count) { $st.Push($c) } } }
  return $out.ToArray() }
$wn.LogoFacts = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  R8 (R35 W7): what the rail logo shows now, for the self-check and the measure part.
  .OUTPUTS
  A table: High (the colors in use: $ui.High), Shown (a logo is on the rail), Other (its pixels with any cover that are
  neither of the 2 system colors of $wn.LogoRole) and Diff (its pixels that differ from the logo in its own colors);
  -1 when no logo is shown.
  #>
  $f = [ordered]@{}; $f['High'] = [bool]$ui.High; $f['Shown'] = $false; $f['Other'] = -1; $f['Diff'] = -1
  $lg = $wn.Logo; if (-not $lg -or -not $lg.Image) { return $f }
  $own = & $wn.LogoImage $false; $d = [string]$wn.LogoRole.Dark; $l = [string]$wn.LogoRole.Light
  try { $f['Shown'] = $true; $f['Other'] = (Get-PfmOtherCount $lg.Image ([Drawing.SystemColors]::$d) ([Drawing.SystemColors]::$l)); $f['Diff'] = (Get-PfmPixelDiff $lg.Image $own) }
  finally { $own.Dispose() }
  return $f }
# R8 (R35 W7): the LAYOUT line for logo facts $F ($wn.LogoFacts) with the wrong colors, or none: with high contrast on,
# a pixel in another color or no change from the own colors; with it off, any pixel that differs from the own colors.
$wn.LogoBad = { param($F)
  if (-not $F.Shown) { return @() }
  if ($F.High -and ([int]$F.Other -ne 0 -or [int]$F.Diff -eq 0)) {
    return @('LAYOUT rail W7 logo: high contrast on, ' + $F.Other + ' pixels not in the system colors, ' + $F.Diff + ' pixels changed from its own colors') }
  if (-not $F.High -and [int]$F.Diff -ne 0) { return @('LAYOUT rail W7 logo: high contrast off, ' + $F.Diff + ' pixels differ from its own colors') }
  return @() }
$wn.HeadFacts = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  The facts of one rail head (R31 W1): the bounds of the logo and the name, their vertical middles and the colors
  behind the logo and behind the panel it sits on.
  .PARAMETER Logo
  The logo picture box.
  .PARAMETER Name
  The app name label.
  .PARAMETER Into
  The panel they sit on (the rail, or the test panel).
  .PARAMETER At
  The scale, as text.
  #>
  param($Logo, $Name, $Into, [string]$At)
  $f = [ordered]@{}; $f['At'] = $At; $f['Logo'] = [string]$Logo.Bounds; $f['Name'] = [string]$Name.Bounds
  $f['LogoMid'] = $Logo.Top + $Logo.Height / 2.0; $f['NameMid'] = $Name.Top + $Name.Height / 2.0
  $f['LogoBack'] = (& $wn.Hex $Logo.BackColor); $f['RailBack'] = (& $wn.Hex $Into.BackColor)
  return $f }
$wn.MeasureHead = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  The rail head at this screen's scale (the rail as built) and at 1.5 x that scale (R31 W1).
  .DESCRIPTION
  For 1.5 x, the same builder ($wn.HeadParts) runs into a navy test panel on the window with the scale ($ui.Dpi) and
  the name's font 1.5 x as large, as Windows makes them at 150 %; then the scale comes back and the panel goes.
  .OUTPUTS
  Two tables of $wn.HeadFacts.
  #>
  $res = @(& $wn.HeadFacts $wn.Logo $wn.AppName $rail ('dpi ' + $ui.Dpi))
  $dpi = $ui.Dpi; $f = $null; $p = $null
  try {
    $wf = $ui.F.Word; $f = New-Object System.Drawing.Font($wf.FontFamily, [single]($wf.Size * 1.5), $wf.Style)
    $ui.Dpi = $dpi * 1.5
    $p = New-Object System.Windows.Forms.Panel; $p.BackColor = $pc.navy; $p.Size = [Drawing.Size]::new((& $wn.Sc 200), (& $wn.Sc 100)); $form.Controls.Add($p)
    $h = & $wn.HeadParts $p $f; [Windows.Forms.Application]::DoEvents()
    $res += & $wn.HeadFacts $h.Logo $h.Name $p ('dpi ' + $ui.Dpi)
  } finally { $ui.Dpi = $dpi; if ($p) { $form.Controls.Remove($p); $p.Dispose() }; if ($f) { $f.Dispose() } }
  return $res }
$wn.MeasureContrast = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  The colors Select-T22Color gives for each palette name with high contrast on and off (R31 W2), with no change of the
  Windows theme.
  .OUTPUTS
  One table per palette name and setting: Table (pc or C), Key, High, System (a system color), Name (its color name),
  Role (the system color its role names), Hex and Own (the window's own color).
  #>
  $rows = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]
  foreach ($t in @(@{ Name = 'pc'; Own = $ui.OwnPc }, @{ Name = 'C'; Own = $ui.OwnC })) {
    foreach ($high in $true, $false) {
      $pick = Select-T22Color $high $t.Own $ui.HcRole
      foreach ($k in @($pick.Keys | Sort-Object)) {
        $r = [ordered]@{}; $r['Table'] = $t.Name; $r['Key'] = [string]$k; $r['High'] = $high; $r['System'] = [bool]$pick[$k].IsSystemColor
        $r['Name'] = [string]$pick[$k].Name; $r['Role'] = [string]$ui.HcRole[$k]; $r['Hex'] = (& $wn.Hex $pick[$k]); $r['Own'] = (& $wn.Hex $t.Own[$k])
        $rows.Add($r) } } }
  return $rows.ToArray() }
$wn.MeasureLogo = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  R8 (R35 W7): the rail logo with high contrast on, then off, with no change of the Windows theme.
  .DESCRIPTION
  The window is recolored both ways ($wn.Recolor with -Force: the rail, the check bar and the card are rebuilt, as on a
  real change of the setting) and the logo facts are taken after each rebuild. Then the window takes the Windows
  setting again.
  .OUTPUTS
  Two tables of $wn.LogoFacts (on, then off), each with When and Bad (the LAYOUT lines of $wn.LogoBad).
  #>
  $res = @()
  try {
    foreach ($h in $true, $false) {
      & $wn.Recolor ('measure ' + $(if ($h) { 'on' } else { 'off' })) $h; [Windows.Forms.Application]::DoEvents()
      $f = & $wn.LogoFacts; $f['When'] = $(if ($h) { 'on' } else { 'off' }); $f['Bad'] = @(& $wn.LogoBad $f); $res += , $f }
  } finally { if ([bool]$ui.High -ne [bool][Windows.Forms.SystemInformation]::HighContrast) { & $wn.Recolor 'measure back' } }
  return $res }
$wn.WheelTry = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  R7 (R32 W2): turns the mouse wheel once towards you (delta -120) at point $Pt of the window, in 2 ways: through the
  window's own handlers (Add-PfmWheel: the MouseWheel event of the control that has the focus, with the pointer in its
  pixels, as Windows sends it), or straight through the routing function on the control tree.
  .PARAMETER Pt
  The pointer, in client pixels of the window ($wn.ViewMid).
  .PARAMETER Focus
  The control the message is for (Windows sends the wheel to the control with the focus).
  .PARAMETER Direct
  When set, the routing function Invoke-PfmWheelRoute is called with $Pt; no event, no screen pixels.
  .OUTPUTS
  @{ Handled (the turn was taken); Under (the control under the pointer: its type and accessible name) }.
  #>
  param($Pt, $Focus, [switch]$Direct)
  $u = Get-PfmWheelUnder $form $Pt
  if ($Direct) { $ok = ($null -ne (Invoke-PfmWheelRoute $form $main $Pt -120)) }
  else { $ok = Send-PfmWheel $Focus $form.PointToScreen($Pt) -120 }
  return @{ Handled = [bool]$ok; Under = ($u.GetType().Name + ' "' + [string]$u.AccessibleName + '"') } }
$wn.WheelCase = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  R7 (R32 W2): one wheel case on Your Work at its top: one turn on the middle of its first card ("Needs You Today"),
  then, when a grid of the card has rows out of view, the card is scrolled to the grid and one turn goes to the middle
  of the grid's part in view ($wn.WheelTry; a button has the focus).
  .PARAMETER Direct
  When set, the turns go straight to the routing function; else through the window's handlers (the Filter key of the result).
  .OUTPUTS
  A table: Scrolls, Point (the pointer, window pixels), PageTop, Under, Handled, Before, After (the main column's
  scroll position) and, when a grid can scroll,
  GridUnder, GridHandled, GridBefore, GridAfter (its first row in view) and MainBefore, MainAfter.
  #>
  param([switch]$Direct)
  $res = [ordered]@{}; $wn.Notice = ''; $wn.Err = ''; & $wn.Show 'home'
  [Windows.Forms.Application]::DoEvents(); $main.AutoScrollPosition = [Drawing.Point]::new(0, 0)
  Add-PfmWheel $form $main; $focus = $(if ($wn.Primary) { $wn.Primary } else { $form })   # the handlers of a normal run ($wn.WheelOn); a new card gets them by ControlAdded
  $sec = @($wn.Secs | Where-Object { $_.Col -eq 0 }) | Select-Object -First 1
  $res['Scrolls'] = [bool]$main.VerticalScroll.Visible; $res['Before'] = -$main.AutoScrollPosition.Y
  $pt = & $wn.ViewMid $sec.Card; $res['Point'] = [string]$pt; $res['PageTop'] = $page.Top
  $t = & $wn.WheelTry $pt $focus -Direct:$Direct
  $res['Under'] = $t.Under; $res['Handled'] = $t.Handled; $res['After'] = -$main.AutoScrollPosition.Y
  $g = @(& $wn.Grids | Where-Object { (Test-PfmGridCanScroll $_ -120) }) | Select-Object -First 1
  if ($g) {
    $main.ScrollControlIntoView($g); [Windows.Forms.Application]::DoEvents()
    $res['MainBefore'] = -$main.AutoScrollPosition.Y; $res['GridBefore'] = $g.FirstDisplayedScrollingRowIndex
    $t = & $wn.WheelTry (& $wn.ViewMid $g) $focus -Direct:$Direct
    $res['GridUnder'] = $t.Under; $res['GridHandled'] = $t.Handled; $res['GridAfter'] = $g.FirstDisplayedScrollingRowIndex; $res['MainAfter'] = -$main.AutoScrollPosition.Y }
  return $res }
$wn.MeasureWheel = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  R7 (R32 W2): proves that the mouse wheel scrolls the card from a point on the card, not on the scroll bar, while a
  button has the focus; and the grid under the pointer while that grid can still scroll.
  .DESCRIPTION
  The window is made 60 % as high so that Your Work scrolls; $wn.WheelCase runs twice: straight through the routing
  function on the control tree (Route: no screen pixels, so it holds for this window off the screen), then through the
  window's own handlers as Windows calls them (Filter). Then the size comes back and Your Work is shown again. No real
  pointer is moved.
  .OUTPUTS
  A table: Card, Route and Filter (each a $wn.WheelCase table).
  #>
  $keep = $form.ClientSize; $res = [ordered]@{}; $res['Card'] = 'home'
  try {
    $form.ClientSize = [Drawing.Size]::new($keep.Width, [int]($keep.Height * 0.6))
    $res['Route'] = (& $wn.WheelCase -Direct); $res['Filter'] = (& $wn.WheelCase)
  } finally { $form.ClientSize = $keep; $wn.Notice = ''; $wn.Err = ''; & $wn.Show 'home'; [Windows.Forms.Application]::DoEvents() }
  return $res }
# The middle of the part of control $C that the main column shows, in client pixels of the window, from the control
# tree (Get-PfmClientOrigin; no screen pixels, so it holds for a window off the screen too). It stops with the places
# when no part shows (R7: an empty overlap gave the point 0,0, on the rail, and hid the cause).
$wn.ViewMid = { param($C)
  $o = Get-PfmClientOrigin $C $form; $mo = Get-PfmClientOrigin $main $form
  $v = [Drawing.Rectangle]::Intersect((New-Object Drawing.Rectangle($o, $C.Size)), (New-Object Drawing.Rectangle($mo, $main.ClientSize)))
  if ($v.Width -lt 1 -or $v.Height -lt 1) { throw ('no part of ' + $C.GetType().Name + ' at ' + $o + ' ' + $C.Size + ' shows in the main column at ' + $mo + ' ' + $main.ClientSize) }
  return [Drawing.Point]::new(($v.Left + [int]($v.Width / 2)), ($v.Top + [int]($v.Height / 2))) }
# The grids on the page (the card shown), in the order they were built.
$wn.Grids = {
  $out = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]; $st = New-Object System.Collections.Queue; $st.Enqueue($page)
  while ($st.Count) { foreach ($c in $st.Dequeue().Controls) { if ($c -is [Windows.Forms.DataGridView]) { $out.Add($c) } elseif ($c.Controls.Count) { $st.Enqueue($c) } } }
  return $out.ToArray() }
$wn.MeasureRun = {
  <#
  .SYNOPSIS
  The -Measure run: builds the window off-screen at 1280 x 720, measures every card, writes the JSON file, closes.
  .DESCRIPTION
  The form is shown far off the screen (it is never seen) so that its controls have handles and can be drawn into
  bitmaps; it builds every card as a normal run does ($wn.Build: layout self-check, accessible names and the card
  pictures, saved next to the JSON file, included), then measures D1 to D4 of every card at 1.25 x and 1.5 x (R6,
  with W1 and W3 of R7), the mouse wheel (R7 W2), the rail head, the high-contrast color choice, (R10) the Feedback
  link with one saved comment and the two own-color logos, and (R8 W7) the logo with high contrast on and off.
  .PARAMETER Path
  The JSON file to write.
  #>
  param([string]$Path)
  $wn.PngDir = Split-Path -Parent $Path
  $form.StartPosition = 'Manual'; $form.ShowInTaskbar = $false; $form.Location = [Drawing.Point]::new(-20000, -20000)
  $form.Show(); [Windows.Forms.Application]::DoEvents()
  & $ui.FormDpi; $ui.Scaled = $true; $form.BackColor = $pc.surface   # R11: as the window part sets it
  $wn.Light = [bool](& $wn.AppsLight)   # R10: the rail logo of this computer's app mode, as $wn.Recolor 'start' sets it in a normal run
  $all = New-Object System.Collections.Generic.List[object]
  # A card that cannot be measured is kept with its error and place, and the run goes on (the test names it).
  & $wn.Build { param($k) try { $all.Add((& $wn.MeasureCard $k)) } catch { $all.Add([ordered]@{ Key = $k; Error = ([string]$_.Exception.Message + ' at ' + (Get-ErrorPlace $_)) }) } }
  # One key per statement: Windows PowerShell 5.1 stopped on the one-literal form ("Argument types do not match", R30 CI).
  $res = [ordered]@{}
  $res['Rev'] = $Rev
  $res['Dpi'] = $ui.Dpi
  $res['Sc8'] = (& $wn.Sc 8)
  $res['Client'] = ([string]$form.ClientSize.Width + 'x' + $form.ClientSize.Height)
  $res['Cards'] = $all.ToArray()
  $res['EmptyNames'] = @($wn.NoName.Keys | ForEach-Object { [string]$_ })
  $res['LayoutDefects'] = @($ui.LayBad)
  $res['Pngs'] = $wn.Pngs.ToArray()
  # R13 (R40): every card opened again shows its kept card (the keep part); a pass that cannot run is kept as its error.
  try { $res['Keep'] = @(& $wn.MeasureKeep) } catch { $res['Keep'] = @(); $res['KeepError'] = ([string]$_.Exception.Message + ' at ' + (Get-ErrorPlace $_)) }
  # D1 to D4 at 1.25 x and 1.5 x (R6; the PFM works at 150 %): every card again; a pass that cannot run is kept as its error.
  try { $res['Scaled'] = @(foreach ($k in 1.25, 1.5) { & $wn.MeasureScaled $k }) }
  catch { $res['Scaled'] = @(); $res['ScaledError'] = ([string]$_.Exception.Message + ' at ' + (Get-ErrorPlace $_)) }
  # R7 (W2): one wheel turn on the card body and one on a grid, through the window's own handlers.
  try { $res['Wheel'] = (& $wn.MeasureWheel) } catch { $res['Wheel'] = $null; $res['WheelError'] = ([string]$_.Exception.Message + ' at ' + (Get-ErrorPlace $_)) }
  # The rail head and the color choice: a step that cannot be measured is kept as its error (the test names it).
  try { $res['Head'] = @(& $wn.MeasureHead) } catch { $res['Head'] = @(); $res['HeadError'] = ([string]$_.Exception.Message + ' at ' + (Get-ErrorPlace $_)) }
  try { $res['Contrast'] = @(& $wn.MeasureContrast) } catch { $res['Contrast'] = @(); $res['ContrastError'] = ([string]$_.Exception.Message + ' at ' + (Get-ErrorPlace $_)) }
  # R10 (R37): the Feedback link and one saved comment (B13); the two own-color logos by app mode.
  try { $res['Feedback'] = (& $wn.MeasureFeedback) } catch { $res['Feedback'] = $null; $res['FeedbackError'] = ([string]$_.Exception.Message + ' at ' + (Get-ErrorPlace $_)) }
  try { $res['Theme'] = (& $wn.MeasureTheme) } catch { $res['Theme'] = $null; $res['ThemeError'] = ([string]$_.Exception.Message + ' at ' + (Get-ErrorPlace $_)) }
  # R8 (R35 W7): the rail logo rebuilt with high contrast on and off (last: it rebuilds the rail, the bar and the card).
  try { $res['Logo'] = @(& $wn.MeasureLogo) } catch { $res['Logo'] = @(); $res['LogoError'] = ([string]$_.Exception.Message + ' at ' + (Get-ErrorPlace $_)) }
  Set-Content -LiteralPath $Path -Value ($res | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 10) -Encoding UTF8
  $form.Close() }
'@ }
